AI.conclusion: Coherence-aware reward fusion can encourage right answers for faithful reasons without architectural changes.

title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL

AI.tldr: ContextPilot teaches agents proactive context management with expanded tools and fine-grained RL. It improves long-context QA and deep search while keeping a more compact working context.
AI.motivation: Existing context-management agents have limited tools, inefficiently explore heterogeneous editing actions, and assign one final reward to all edits.
AI.method: ContextPilot adds planning, long-term-memory, and soft-offloading tools, then branches on actions identified by context and entropy variation and estimates action-level advantages from traversing trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments on long-context QA and deep-search tasks show stronger performance and more compact working context than existing baselines across base models and benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Specialized tools and action-level credit assignment enable more effective proactive context control for long-horizon agents.

title: From Agent Skills to Executable Environments: Frontier-Targeted Training for Tool-Use LLMs

AI.tldr: Grafting converts agent skills into validated executable tool-use environments, and Fathoming trains on capability-frontier trajectories. The resulting 4B model makes large out-of-distribution gains on tool-use benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Tool-use LLM training lacks scalable stateful environments and verified multi-turn trajectories matched to a target model's current capability boundary.
AI.method: Grafting has coding-agent harnesses build and refine executable environments under deterministic validation; Fathoming iteratively applies GRPO to verified near-frontier trajectories.
AI.result: Grafting produces 500 environments and about 12K trajectories; Fathom-4B raises BFCLv4 multi-turn accuracy from 22.0 to 39.7 and ComplexFuncBench per-call accuracy from 49.6 to 61.6. The pipeline also creates 5,101-environment Grove-5K.
AI.conclusion: Agent skills can seed scalable verified environments and frontier-targeted trajectories for improving tool-use LLMs.

title: HiEvi-RAG: Hierarchical Evidence-Driven Reasoning for Long Document Understanding

AI.tldr: HiEvi-RAG is a hierarchical evidence-driven multimodal RAG framework for closed-domain long-document understanding. Across four benchmarks, it surpasses the prior state of the art by an average 8.05% accuracy.
AI.motivation: Semantic retrievers can retrieve answer-void topical distractors, and single-pass RAG cascades errors when initial retrieval misses key evidence.
AI.method: The framework decomposes a complex query into child questions, performs coarse multimodal page retrieval, uses the GRPO-trained EviAgent to verify pages across multi-image blocks, and iteratively generates answers using accumulated sub-question memory.
AI.result: Evaluations on four benchmarks show that HiEvi-RAG outperforms existing open-source baselines and improves accuracy over the previous state of the art by 8.05% on average.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical decomposition, evidence verification, and memory-guided iterative reasoning provide complementary gains for multimodal long-document RAG.

title: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents

AI.tldr: ICA assigns credit to information acquired during long-horizon web-agent trajectories using visually grounded webpage snapshots. Combined with GSPO, it consistently improves results on four information-seeking benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Terminal rewards show whether an answer is correct but not which intermediate information enabled it, while text-parsed webpages are incomplete and unstable across trajectories.
AI.method: ICA represents fetched webpages as rendered snapshots and estimates each information unit's turn-level utility from rollout success rates, then propagates dense rewards to steps that introduced high-utility evidence.
AI.result: Integrated with GSPO, ICA consistently improves performance on BrowseComp, GAIA, Xbench-DS, and Seal-0.
AI.conclusion: Stable, identifiable visual evidence units enable more informative credit assignment for long-horizon information-seeking agents.

title: GTS: Inference-Time Scaling of Latent Reasoning with a Learnable Gaussian Thought Sampler

AI.tldr: GTS replaces heuristic latent-reasoning perturbations with a learned, context-dependent Gaussian sampler. It consistently improves pass@N over heuristic baselines across two backbones and multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Dropout and fixed Gaussian noise can cause distribution shifts without yielding useful candidate reasoning paths because they are not optimizable or context-conditioned.
AI.method: GTS predicts Gaussian perturbations over continuous reasoning states and is trained with GRPO-style policy optimization while keeping the latent-reasoning backbone frozen.
AI.result: Across two latent reasoning backbones and several benchmarks, GTS consistently improves pass@N relative to heuristic perturbation baselines.
AI.conclusion: Effective inference-time scaling for latent reasoning needs controlled, trainable exploration rather than stronger fixed stochasticity.

title: Reward-Decomposed Reinforcement Learning for Immersive Video Role-Playing

AI.tldr: EBM-RL trains video-grounded role-playing dialogue through separately optimized perception, reasoning, and response stages. It outperforms text-only and comparable-scale VLM baselines while transferring zero-shot to VideoQA.
AI.motivation: Text-only role-playing models often miss visual scene atmosphere and evolving tension needed for immersive VR games and interactive narratives.
AI.method: The GRPO-based Eye-Brain-Mouth framework separates perception, thinking, and answer generation, and combines rewards for scene-text alignment, perceptual-cognitive utility, answer faithfulness, and format consistency.
AI.result: EBM-RL substantially outperforms text-only role-playing and comparable-scale VLM baselines, remains competitive with larger VLMs on visual grounding and situational persona, and transfers zero-shot to out-of-domain VideoQA.
AI.conclusion: Reward-decomposed See-Think-Speak training can make role-playing dialogue more visually grounded and immersive.

title: Gradient Starvation in Low-Rank Language Model Pretraining

AI.tldr: This study identifies gradient starvation as a partial explanation for low-rank pretraining's representational gap from full-rank models. Representational alignment predicts downstream competence better than perplexity in the reported experiments.
AI.motivation: Low-rank pretraining underperforms full-rank pretraining, but it is unclear whether the persistent gap comes from initialization, factorization, or training dynamics.
AI.method: Using GPT-2 on BabyLM, the authors manipulate spectrum-matched initialization and gradient dimensionality, then compare representation alignment, perplexity, and downstream competence.
AI.result: Spectrum-matched initialization removes the step-zero gap but it reappears within a few steps; changing gradient dimensionality directly changes full-rank alignment independent of weight rank. Spectral normalization can improve perplexity without restoring alignment.
AI.conclusion: Gradient starvation is a genuine partial mechanism, and efficient pretraining should assess both representational trajectories and task performance.

title: LQ-Rewriter: Generative Reward Model-Guided Lazy Query Rewriting for Role-Playing Dialogue

AI.tldr: LQ-Rewriter turns short, ambiguous role-playing inputs into richer queries using a preference-trained generative reward model. It achieves the strongest GRM-based and human preference win rates among the tested rewriting baselines and improves online deployment.
AI.motivation: Lazy role-playing queries lack explicit intent and emotion, while existing rewriting methods target functional tasks rather than character consistency and user preferences.
AI.method: A listwise GRM is trained from online regeneration preferences to provide process and final signals; rejection fine-tuning and reinforcement learning train LQ-Rewriter to enrich inputs while preserving intent and context.
AI.result: On real dialogue logs from a mainstream Chinese romantic role-playing platform, the GRM beats general-purpose LLM judges and LQ-Rewriter attains the highest GRM-based and human-preference win rates among baselines.
AI.conclusion: Role-playing-specific preference supervision can make rewriting underspecified user inputs more engaging without losing their intended meaning.

title: VerTox: Verifiable Reward-Guided Corpus Poisoning Against Neural Ranking Models

AI.tldr: VerTox uses verifiable reward-guided reinforcement learning to generate corpus-poisoning documents against neural rankers. Its fluent, low-perplexity documents achieve near-perfect attack success rates and harm a downstream RAG application.
AI.motivation: Neural ranking systems are vulnerable to scalable, deceptive LLM-generated corpus documents, but this threat is not well understood.
AI.method: VerTox fine-tunes compact LLMs with RLVR, using reward shaping that jointly encourages ranking distortion and factual corruption.
AI.result: The attack achieves near-perfect success rates across major neural ranking architectures and a proprietary commercial embedding model; its documents frequently outrank targets and significantly degrade a downstream RAG application.
AI.conclusion: Reward-guided LLM generation can create hard-to-detect corpus-poisoning attacks, exposing a serious robustness risk for neural retrieval and RAG systems.

title: BiMTokenizer: Preserving Semantic-Acoustic Balance in Low-Bitrate Speech Tokenization via Bidirectional State-Space Modeling

AI.tldr: BiMTokenizer is a roughly 1.1 kbps single-tower speech codec that combines bidirectional state-space modeling with Residual Spherical Leech Quantization. It yields better reconstruction and the lowest WER among low-bitrate codec baselines while using less than half as many parameters as recent dual-tower models.
AI.motivation: Low-bitrate speech tokenization must balance acoustic fidelity and semantic preservation, whereas dual-tower solutions add substantial architectural overhead.
AI.method: BiMTokenizer uses a bidirectional state-space backbone for temporal modeling and RSLQ, a fixed well-separated lattice bottleneck that avoids learned-codebook collapse.
AI.result: It achieves superior acoustic reconstruction and the lowest WER across clean and noisy conditions, uses less than half the parameters of recent dual-tower baselines, and performs strongly on downstream speech understanding.
AI.conclusion: A carefully designed single-tower codec can preserve semantic and acoustic information at low bitrates without dual-tower complexity.

title: Enhancing LLMs in Predictive Political QA with Semi-Structured Data

AI.tldr: PSL improves predictive political QA by extracting both actor stances and higher-order political interaction structure from semi-structured records. It consistently outperforms baselines across three real-world datasets and multiple LLMs.
AI.motivation: Political resources rarely contain predictive answers directly, and existing LLM augmentation methods under-model signals that reveal preferences and dependencies among actors.
AI.method: PSL forms a semantic view that extracts question-relevant actor stances and a vector view that learns structure-aware actor representations from an interaction graph.
AI.result: Across three real-world datasets and multiple LLMs, PSL consistently outperforms baselines; ablations confirm complementary gains from stance and structure signals.
AI.conclusion: Turning semi-structured political records into stance and relational evidence improves LLM-based political prediction.

title: Not All Prompts Are Equal: Exploration-Guided Prompt Scaffolding for Multimodal Reinforcement Post-Training

AI.tldr: This work dynamically scaffolds multimodal RL training prompts according to their exploration value rather than allocating equal rollouts to all prompts. It improves in-domain performance by up to 9.7% relatively and gains 11.5% on MathVision and 11.1% on MMMU-Pro.
AI.motivation: Standard online RL gives equal rollout budget to saturated prompts and overly difficult prompts, although both provide weak learning signals.
AI.method: The framework calculates an Exploration Potential Score from on-policy rollout statistics, then uses a teacher to rewrite low-utility prompts while preserving task intent and trains with GRPO.
AI.result: On Geo3K and MMK12, the method consistently beats the baseline in-domain and out-of-distribution, with up to 9.7% relative in-domain improvement, 11.5% on MathVision, and 11.1% on MMMU-Pro.
AI.conclusion: Refining prompt difficulty based on rollout-derived utility can make multimodal RL post-training more informative.

title: Ada-DeVL: Adaptive Decoupling of Visual and Logical Reasoning Pathways for Efficient MLLMs

AI.tldr: Ada-DeVL adaptively separates visual perception depth from logical reasoning intensity in MLLMs. It improves MMMU accuracy while substantially reducing token use.
AI.motivation: Uniformly applying deep visual analysis and long reasoning to every query wastes tokens and causes overthinking.
AI.method: Ada-DeVL selects one of four visuo-reasoning pathways based on problem complexity, using self-distillation SFT for difficulty-aligned data followed by GRPO with diversity and format rewards.
AI.result: On MMMU, Qwen2.5-VL-7B Ada-DeVL reaches 54.0% accuracy while saving 39.6% tokens; Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 64.0%, reduces tokens by 44.6%, and averages 1560.8 versus 4889.0 tokens for Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling and adapting perception and reasoning effort can maintain or improve MLLM accuracy with much lower inference cost.

title: Do MLLMs Really See It: Reinforcing Visual Attention in Multimodal LLMs

AI.tldr: SAYO trains MLLMs with a region-level visual-attention reward to make visual reasoning more reliably grounded. It consistently improves diverse reasoning and perception benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Long textual chain-of-thought does not ensure stable visual attention, so early visual misalignment often propagates into failed inferences.
AI.method: SAYO uses reinforcement learning with a region-level visual-attention-based reward that aligns optimization signals with visually grounded reasoning steps.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple multimodal benchmarks show consistent improvements on diverse reasoning and perception tasks.
AI.conclusion: Explicit credit assignment for visual attention can improve how well MLLMs attend to relevant image regions during reasoning.

title: Peak-Then-Collapse and the Four Interface Channels of Knowledge-Graph Tool Use

AI.tldr: This work finds a reproducible peak-then-collapse failure in RLVR knowledge-graph tool use and attributes it to sparse interface feedback. One-iteration self-distillation reaches 40 EM, while the best 14B model reaches 40.2 EM.
AI.motivation: Standard RLVR succeeds with interfaces whose errors expose familiar natural-language feedback, but its behavior on minimal knowledge-graph APIs is poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors train GRPO on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct using four Freebase navigation verbs over Complex WebQuestions, compare seven reward designs, conduct oracle relation ablations, and test self-distillation and scaling.
AI.result: Correct-via-tool rate rises from 3.8 to 9.6 over 250 steps then falls to zero within 50 steps across four seeds; 95.4% of retrieval-dependent errors are retrieval-composition failures, and gold relations add only 0.20 pp exact match.
AI.conclusion: For this interface, reward redesign and moderate scaling do not solve an interface-bound degradation regime caused by uninformative feedback.

title: PAPO: Stabilizing Rubric Integration Training via Decoupled Advantage Normalization

AI.tldr: PAPO adds process-level supervision to GRPO without the verbosity-driven reward hacking of direct process rewards. It reaches 51.3% versus 46.3% on OlympiadBench for Qwen2.5-7B and continues improving after ORM plateaus.
AI.motivation: Outcome rewards cannot distinguish correct responses and lose signal when groups are all correct, while direct process-reward optimization can reward verbosity and collapse accuracy.
AI.method: PAPO combines an outcome advantage normalized across all responses with a process advantage normalized only within correct responses, preserving correctness while retaining process-level gradients.
AI.result: PAPO consistently outperforms ORM across five model configurations and six benchmarks, including 51.3% versus 46.3% on OlympiadBench for Qwen2.5-7B.
AI.conclusion: Decoupled advantage normalization can safely integrate rubric-based process evaluation into GRPO.

title: A Novel Semantic Manifold Alignment Attack against Embedding-to-Embedding Obfuscation in Privacy-Preserving LLMs

AI.tldr: PMA attacks Embedding-to-Embedding Obfuscation privacy schemes by reconstructing plaintext from an obfuscated vector stream. It consistently recovers more plaintext than prior attack methods.
AI.motivation: E2EO schemes preserve semantic structure through large-scale substitution but offer no cryptographic guarantee, despite resisting token-frequency and embedding-inversion attacks.
AI.method: PMA treats obfuscated vectors as an unknown tokenizer language, learns separate Word2Vec proxy embeddings for ciphertext and public text, aligns their manifolds by structural similarity, and maps vectors back to plaintext.
AI.result: Experiments show that PMA consistently achieves higher plaintext recovery than state-of-the-art attack methods.
AI.conclusion: Preserved semantic geometry can leak enough information to undermine lightweight embedding obfuscation schemes.

title: From Rollouts to Recipes: Self-Contained Post-Training for LLMs

AI.tldr: Self-Routing adapts LLM post-training recipes to a sample's rollout correctness and confidence. It consistently outperforms uniform GRPO, uniform OPSD, fixed mixtures, and simpler routing baselines on mathematical reasoning.
AI.motivation: A single post-training recipe ignores the distinct sample-level learning states revealed by a model's own rollouts.
AI.method: Based on behavioral state, Self-Routing routes samples to GRPO, on-policy self-distillation, regularization, or skipping, without external teachers, annotations, or extra sampling.
AI.result: Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 mathematical-reasoning experiments, Self-Routing consistently improves over uniform and fixed-mixture alternatives; routing changes throughout training and reduces unnecessary low-signal updates.
AI.conclusion: Rollout-conditioned routing can allocate post-training updates more effectively than applying one recipe to every sample.

title: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation

AI.tldr: PGPO protects LLM-enhanced recommender embeddings from inversion while preserving their relational topology. On two benchmarks, it provides strong inversion defense with recommendation performance near the upper bound.
AI.motivation: Existing input-side privacy defenses can disrupt the inter-item semantic topology needed for recommendation.
AI.method: PGPO learns topology-aware obfuscation anchors for influential prototype words, propagates them through a static semantic graph, and optimizes individual dissimilarity, structural consistency, and semantic constraint rewards with GRPO.
AI.result: Experiments on two benchmarks show strong inversion defense while maintaining near-upper-bound recommendation performance.
AI.conclusion: Preserving relative item relationships while shifting semantic content is a viable privacy-utility objective for LLM-enhanced recommendation.

title: The Weakest Link Tells It All: Outcome-Supervised Process Reward Modeling via Learnable Credit Assignment

AI.tldr: LCA trains outcome-supervised process reward models by learning which reasoning steps deserve credit under a weakest-link principle. It outperforms prior outcome-supervised PRMs across multiple tasks and backbones.
AI.motivation: Stepwise process annotations are expensive, and existing outcome-supervised credit assignment does not anchor credit in step correctness, limiting error identification.
AI.method: LCA formulates outcome-supervised PRM training as multiple-instance learning and uses Softmax-Weighted-Sum pooling to jointly learn credit assignment and step rewards under Weakest Link Assignment.
AI.result: The authors establish instance-level Bayes consistency under mild assumptions and report better performance than state-of-the-art outcome-supervised PRMs across tasks and backbones.
AI.conclusion: Learnable weakest-link credit assignment offers a scalable route to more useful process rewards from final outcomes alone.

title: FlexiSLM: A Spoken Language Model with Dynamic and Controllable Frame Rates

AI.tldr: FlexiSLM is the first spoken language model with dynamic, controllable frame rates. At 6.25 Hz it roughly halves inference time versus 12.5 Hz while retaining strong speech-to-speech quality.
AI.motivation: Fixed-frame-rate spoken language models ignore time-varying speech information density and limit quality-speed tradeoffs.
AI.method: FlexiSLM integrates pretrained FlexiCodec dynamic output tokens into a multitask speech-to-speech SLM, adds input-side frame compression, and conditions directly on requested frame rate.
AI.result: It outperforms fixed-frame-rate 7B models including Qwen2.5-Omni and Kimi-Audio at 12.5 and 6.25 Hz, can operate at 4.0 Hz, and approximately halves inference time at 6.25 Hz relative to 12.5 Hz.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic frame-rate tokenization gives spoken language models controllable efficiency without sacrificing strong output quality.

title: TopoAlign: A Framework for Aligning Code to Math via Topological Decomposition

AI.tldr: TopoAlign converts code repositories into structurally analogous training data for formal mathematics. It substantially improves reported autoformalization metrics despite adding no mathematical knowledge.
AI.motivation: Informal-to-formal math translation lacks large paired corpora, while abundant code does not transfer directly because its structure and syntax differ from formal mathematics.
AI.method: TopoAlign decomposes code into docstrings, main functions, and dependency functions, then reassembles them into structures mirroring formal statements.
AI.result: The method improves one reported model by 17.77% on BEq@10 and 68.82% on typecheck@10, and another by 0.12% and 1.09%, respectively, without new mathematical knowledge.
AI.conclusion: Structurally aligned code data can expand training resources for mathematical autoformalization.

title: Beyond SFT-Optimality: Cold-Start Data Selection for Reinforcement Learning via Gradient Subspace Coverage

AI.tldr: RL-Proxy-Coverage selects cold-start SFT data for downstream RL by covering a reward-relevant gradient subspace. It outperforms SFT-centric, hard-diverse, and reward-aware selectors at early-to-mid RL checkpoints in mathematical reasoning.
AI.motivation: Stronger SFT initialization does not necessarily produce a better starting point for RLVR because cold-start data also shapes downstream update geometry.
AI.method: The method estimates a low-rank gradient subspace from representative RL prompts and verifier rewards, then selects SFT examples with non-redundant gradient coverage of that subspace.
AI.result: In controlled mathematical-reasoning experiments, RL-Proxy-Coverage beats representative SFT-centric, hard-diverse, and reward-aware baselines at early-to-mid RL checkpoints.
AI.conclusion: Cold-start data should be selected as an initialization resource for reward optimization, not only for supervised learning quality.

title: Expanding the Solvable Frontier: Policy-Adaptive Curriculum Learning for Reasoning RL

AI.tldr: PAD-Curriculum estimates a reasoning model's evolving solvable frontier and adapts GRPO training data accordingly. It consistently improves over standard GRPO and curriculum or distillation baselines on GSM8K, MATH, and NuminaMath-CoT.
AI.motivation: Static difficulty measures misrepresent RL learning value: currently unsolved problems may be too sparse for learning, while greedily solved problems can still generate useful stochastic trajectories.
AI.method: PAD-Curriculum ranks solved problems by normalized Scorer-to-Student KL discrepancy against a frozen stronger scorer, defers unsolved problems, and periodically re-evaluates them as the policy improves.
AI.result: Across Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 models on GSM8K, MATH, and NuminaMath-CoT, it consistently outperforms standard GRPO and curriculum or distillation baselines, especially on harder reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Policy-adaptive discrepancy estimates are more useful for curriculum construction than static scorer-based difficulty.

title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment

AI.tldr: SafeSteer preserves general LLM capabilities during safety alignment by distilling only safety-relevant output tokens. It beats prior methods on seven safety benchmarks with minimal degradation on five general-capability benchmarks using only 100 harmful samples.
AI.motivation: Safety alignment often imposes an alignment tax, and existing approaches rely on large general datasets or auxiliary reward models.
AI.method: SafeSteer builds a safety teacher through activation steering, selects safety tokens, and restricts the reverse-KL distillation penalty to those tokens.
AI.result: Across diverse models, it outperforms existing methods on seven safety benchmarks with minimal degradation on five general benchmarks, requiring only 100 harmful examples and less than 1% of the general-purpose data used by previous baselines.
AI.conclusion: Localized changes to safety-relevant tokens can reduce alignment cost and capability loss.

title: MDM-Prime-v2: Binary Encoding and Index Shuffling Enable Scaling of Diffusion Language Models

AI.tldr: MDM-Prime-v2 improves masked diffusion language models through Binary Encoding and Index Shuffling. At 1.1B parameters, it achieves the best average zero-shot accuracy among the listed similarly sized baselines across eight commonsense benchmarks.
AI.motivation: MDM-Prime's BPE subtokenizer can inflate the training objective, and its token-granularity choice lacks principled guidance.
AI.method: The authors analyze subtokenizer designs that minimize the MDM-Prime objective, characterize the role of granularity and sub-token entropy, and introduce Binary Encoding plus Index Shuffling.
AI.result: When scaled to 1.1B parameters, MDM-Prime-v2 outperforms GPT-Neo, OPT, Pythia, Bloom, SMDM, and TinyLLaMA in average zero-shot accuracy over eight commonsense reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Principled subtokenizer design can improve both masked diffusion training objectives and downstream language-model performance.

title: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal

AI.tldr: Embedded activation steering can lose its behavioral effect after downstream fine-tuning even when the underlying weight edit is barely reversed. Refusal ablation loses 69% of its effect under the reported SFT setup but only 2% under RLHF.
AI.motivation: It is unknown whether activation steering embedded in weights survives the routine fine-tuning that follows model deployment.
AI.method: The study evaluates embedded refusal-ablation and brevity-amplification steering across five 3B-14B instruction-tuned models under non-adversarial SFT and RLHF.
AI.result: Stronger optimization against the steered behavior causes more degradation; SFT removes 69% of refusal-ablation effect on average versus 2% for RLHF, while only 0.4% of the weight edit is restored and update directions are nearly orthogonal to the edit.
AI.conclusion: Fine-tuning can recover behavior without undoing the corresponding weight edit, so embedded steering needs validation after downstream training.

title: Natural Language to First-Order Logic LLM-based Autoformalization

AI.tldr: This paper defines and surveys LLM-based natural-language-to-first-order-logic autoformalization. It separates ontology extraction from logical translation and identifies key open problems for the field.
AI.motivation: First-order-logic autoformalization lacks a unified task formulation and systematic survey, making cross-study evaluation unclear.
AI.method: The paper distinguishes Ontology Extraction and Logical Translation, reviews datasets, metrics, and methods including fine-tuning, prompting, and verification-based refinement, and analyzes open challenges.
AI.result: The work provides a principled task definition and survey, identifying challenges in benchmarking, semantic evaluation, ontology-aware methods, and end-to-end applications.
AI.conclusion: Separating ontology extraction from logical translation is necessary for clearer evaluation and progress in FOL autoformalization.

title: P-Search: A Parallel Plan–Act–Verify Framework with Decoupled GRPO for Deep Research

AI.tldr: P-Search organizes open-web deep research into parallel, independently verifiable evidence branches. Its trained 8B Plan plus ReAct system reaches 59.2% on GAIA and 70.0% on Xbench-DeepSearch.
AI.motivation: Single-path ReAct and long-context search can overexplore one hypothesis while missing alternative entities, constraints, and falsifying evidence.
AI.method: P-Search builds grounded context, decomposes tasks into parallel branches, runs branch-specific search agents, and verifies unresolved constraints; separate ReAct and Plan components are trained with star-shaped data and role-specific GRPO rewards.
AI.result: P-Search improves reported baselines for GLM-5 and Tongyi-DR-30B on most open-web benchmarks, while its trained 8B system reaches 59.2% on GAIA and 70.0% on Xbench-DeepSearch. Ablations support complementary Plan, ReAct, and Verify roles.
AI.conclusion: Parallel planning, execution, and verification offer a scalable structure for evidence-based deep-research agents.

title: Dual-View Training for Instruction-Following Information Retrieval

AI.tldr: Dual-view training improves instruction-following retrieval by generating polarity-reversed relevance views. It raises FollowIR p-MRR from 5.27 to 8.30 for a 305M encoder at a matched 880k-example budget.
AI.motivation: Instruction-following retrievers must satisfy topical intent and instance-specific constraints, but training can leave representations insensitive to instructions.
AI.method: Given an instruction-relevant and an instruction-excluded topical document, an LLM creates a complementary instruction that reverses their relevance labels, yielding paired views that penalize instruction-agnostic representations.
AI.result: For a 305M encoder, p-MRR rises from 5.27 to 8.30 and instruction-conditioned Score from 20.85 to 21.38; gains repeat at 560M, improve InfoSearch nDCG@5, and do not degrade average performance on four BEIR datasets.
AI.conclusion: Label reversal, rather than extra generated wording, provides useful supervision for instruction-sensitive retrieval.

title: Gradients Know What Outcomes Don’t: Unlocking Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning with Gradient-Aligned Rewards

AI.tldr: GAR provides dense reasoning rewards by matching each rollout's output-layer gradient to an expert-anchor gradient. It improves over GRPO and other baselines on math and transfers to GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro with under 9% wall-clock overhead.
AI.motivation: Binary RLVR outcome rewards cannot distinguish correct trajectories, while dense alternatives either ignore expert solutions or need costly offline labels.
AI.method: GAR extracts a compact gradient vector using truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer and uses its cosine similarity to an expert-anchor gradient as reward; the cosine is decomposed into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors.
AI.result: On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, GAR consistently improves competition-level math results over GRPO and other baselines, transfers to GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro, and adds less than 9% wall-clock overhead.
AI.conclusion: Gradient-space alignment with available expert solutions can supply efficient, reasoning-aware dense rewards.

title: AWARe: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting via Activation-Weighted Adaptive REtention

AI.tldr: AWARe mitigates catastrophic forgetting in MLLM fine-tuning by freezing parameters according to activation-based importance. It preserves upstream capabilities while outperforming existing methods on downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: Downstream fine-tuning overwrites parameters important to multimodal pretraining, degrading earlier capabilities and limiting deployment.
AI.method: AWARe assigns activation-based importance scores to parameters, selectively freezes those needed for prior knowledge, and updates less important ones without modifying model architecture.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that AWARe preserves upstream capabilities and achieves superior downstream performance compared with existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Activation patterns can guide selective parameter retention to reduce catastrophic forgetting without changing inference architecture.

title: MathDebugger: A Benchmark for Type-Aware Error Detection in Synthetic Math Data

AI.tldr: MathDebugger is a 6,000-item type-aware benchmark for detecting and classifying errors in synthetic mathematical questions and answers. Even leading LLMs and process reward models remain far from saturated, especially on fine-grained error types.
AI.motivation: Synthetic math data is widely used for LLM training but may contain errors, and existing evaluation does not jointly assess detection and error-type classification.
AI.method: The benchmark includes 2,000 correct questions, 2,000 erroneous questions across four error types, and 2,000 annotated answers including 610 erroneous ones across three types, with correctness and type labels.
AI.result: Per-error-type Fleiss' kappa is 0.69-0.88; across 14 LLMs and three process reward models, systems struggle particularly with fine-grained types, and error-type supervision significantly improves correction under paired bootstrap testing.
AI.conclusion: Synthetic-math verification is substantially harder than solving, and type-aware labels offer actionable supervision for correction.

title: Cognitive-Level Prefix-MoE Reward Modeling for Curriculum Alignment of Medical Language Models

AI.tldr: Prefix-MoE RM aligns medical language models across recall, analysis, decision, and synthesis using specialized prefix experts and curriculum GRPO. It raises reward-model pairwise accuracy from 79.8 to 93.0 and the Qwen3-32B system reaches 50.1 HealthBench and 4.55 LLMEval-Med.
AI.motivation: A single reward score conflicts across different clinical reasoning abilities, while answer-key-based medical RL mainly rewards multiple-choice correctness rather than open-ended reasoning.
AI.method: Prefix-MoE RM routes query-response pairs through cognitive-level prefix experts, softly fuses trainable prefixes into one reward, trains on non-multiple-choice preferences, and supports mixed-data curriculum GRPO with answer-key feedback.
AI.result: Pairwise accuracy improves from 79.8 to 93.0 over a shared RM; replacing Prefix-MoE with a shared RM or soft expert-head MoE lowers HealthBench from 43.8 to 24.8 and 34.6. The Qwen3-8B system beats Qwen3-32B base on MedXpertQA and HealthBench.
AI.conclusion: Cognitive-level expert routing can reduce reward conflicts and strengthen open-ended medical reasoning while retaining exam-style performance.

title: LLaDA-Rec: Discrete Diffusion for Parallel Semantic ID Generation in Generative Recommendation

AI.tldr: LLaDA-Rec uses discrete diffusion to generate recommendation semantic IDs in parallel rather than autoregressively. It consistently outperforms conventional ID-based recommenders and strong generative baselines on three public datasets.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive semantic-ID generation is constrained to left-to-right dependencies and accumulates early token errors, hurting recommendation accuracy.
AI.method: LLaDA-Rec combines diffusion-compatible parallel SID tokenization, user-history and next-item masking, bidirectional attention, adaptive generation order, and adapted beam-search decoding.
AI.result: Across three public datasets, LLaDA-Rec consistently outperforms conventional ID-based recommenders and strong generative recommendation baselines.
AI.conclusion: Parallel discrete diffusion is a promising alternative to autoregressive semantic-ID generation for recommendation.

title: EDGE: Experience-Distillation for Guided Exploration in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: EDGE uses retrieved experiences as temporary training scaffolds and distills their benefits into an evolving agent policy. It improves strong RL baselines by up to 12.5 points and remains effective without inference-time scaffolds.
AI.motivation: Exploration patterns in RL trajectories are discarded after one update, while inference-time experience retrieval can become stale and create permanent external dependencies.
AI.method: EDGE compares experience-conditioned and experience-free trajectories within a rollout group to admit positive marginal gains, distills behavior with reverse KL on empirical support, and co-evolves an experience bank that adds failure-driven guidance and prunes obsolete entries.
AI.result: Across embodied, web, and search-based QA tasks, EDGE improves over strong RL baselines by up to 12.5 points and works without inference-time scaffolds or a proprietary reflector.
AI.conclusion: Distilling useful experiences during training can improve exploration without retaining external retrieval dependencies at inference.

title: POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories

AI.tldr: POLARIS trains Qwen3.5-9B for long-form story writing using an LLM judge and human-reference injection. It is competitive with larger open-weight models, follows length requests better, and remains strong on requests up to three times its training-story length.
AI.motivation: Small open-weight models often underwrite requested stories or lose quality as generated length grows.
AI.method: POLARIS applies a lower-compute GRPO recipe with a frontier LLM's structured Story Quality rubric as reward and teacher-forced human stories as high-reward anchors; it trains Qwen3.5-9B on about 1.4K prompt-story pairs using four A100 GPUs.
AI.result: Across five benchmarks, POLARIS-9B is competitive with larger open-weight models and is preferred over base Qwen3.5-9B in blinded human evaluation while matching Qwen3.5-27B. It preserves quality for prompts requesting up to three times the training length.
AI.conclusion: Length generalization is a meaningful stress test for creative-writing models, and anchored reference injection can help small models meet it.

title: World Models for Policy Refinement in StarCraft II

AI.tldr: StarWM learns action-conditioned textual world models for StarCraft II and uses them to refine an LLM agent's policy. StarWM-Agent gains 30%, 15%, and 30% win rate against Hard, Harder, and VeryHard built-in AI, respectively.
AI.motivation: LLM-based StarCraft II agents improve policies directly but have not systematically integrated learnable action-conditioned dynamics models for foresight.
AI.method: StarWM predicts short-horizon player-view future observations under partial observability, and StarWM-Agent applies it in a Generate-Simulate-Refine loop for policy refinement.
AI.result: StarWM outperforms zero-shot baselines across multiple dimensions; StarWM-Agent achieves 30%, 15%, and 30% win-rate gains against Hard LV5, Harder LV6, and VeryHard LV7 AI. Combining it with history summarization yields the strongest online performance.
AI.conclusion: Learnable textual world models can provide useful foresight for policy refinement in partially observable StarCraft II.

title: GPAgentBench-2K: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Complex Clinical Action Space

AI.tldr: GPAgentBench-2K benchmarks LLM clinical agents in a constrained primary-care action space with safety-aware abstention. It finds that even frontier models violate safety constraints in over half of high-risk cases.
AI.motivation: Existing clinical-agent benchmarks simplify workflows into static predictions or unconstrained MDPs with coarse action sets.
AI.method: The benchmark uses expert-validated general-practice encounter records to define a CMDP with six foundational actions, a topological workflow prior, and safety-informed abstention; it evaluates 16 LLMs and establishes a C-GRPO reference.
AI.result: Performance drops substantially as the action space expands, and frontier models with the highest diagnosis accuracy still violate safety constraints in more than half of high-risk cases. C-GRPO improves over unconstrained RL but remains far from clinically acceptable safety.
AI.conclusion: Clinical LLM agents face a pronounced quality-safety gap that constrained optimization alone does not yet solve.

title: Think, Act, Build: An Agentic Framework with Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding

AI.tldr: TAB performs zero-shot 3D visual grounding directly from RGB-D streams through dynamic VLM-guided 2D-to-3D reconstruction. Using only open-source models, it significantly outperforms prior zero-shot and even supervised baselines on ScanRefer and Nr3D.
AI.motivation: Existing zero-shot 3D grounding methods rely on processed point clouds and pretrained 3D detectors, reducing grounding to static proposal matching.
AI.method: TAB uses 2D VLMs for spatial semantics and multi-view geometry for 3D construction, dynamically tracks targets in frames, and applies Semantic-Anchored Geometric Expansion from a reference clip to unobserved views; it also refines benchmark ambiguities and category errors.
AI.result: On ScanRefer and Nr3D, TAB with entirely open-source models significantly outperforms previous zero-shot methods and supervised baselines.
AI.conclusion: Agentic visual-tool use plus semantic-anchored geometric expansion can make zero-shot 3D grounding more capable and robust.

title: CogniDir: Combating Cognitive Malicious Comments via Adaptive Distributional Learning for Robust Fake News Detection

AI.tldr: CogniDir improves fake-news robustness against cognitively manipulative LLM-generated comments by adaptively reweighting attack-specific training data. It improves F1 by up to 17.9% over competitive baselines across three benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Psychologically grounded malicious comments manipulate cognition and logic rather than surface text, undermining detectors trained under fixed attack assumptions and distributions.
AI.method: CogniDir formalizes cognitive adversarial paradigms, computes an information-theoretic score from accuracy and confidence, parameterizes it as a Dirichlet prior, and adaptively reallocates training exposure toward brittle mechanisms.
AI.result: Across three benchmarks, CogniDir achieves state-of-the-art robustness and improves F1 by up to 17.9% over competitive baselines under heterogeneous AI-generated attacks.
AI.conclusion: Feedback-driven optimization of attack-mixture exposure can improve robustness to diverse cognitive manipulation strategies.

title: The RAT: A Unified Bayesian Model for RAG Evaluation

AI.tldr: The RAT is a Bayesian framework that jointly evaluates retrieval success, abstention, and answer correctness in RAG systems. It reveals behavior differences hidden by marginal metrics and incorporates calibrated LLM-as-a-judge annotations.
AI.motivation: End-to-end RAG metrics do not show how retrieval, abstention, and generation interact or how component errors propagate.
AI.method: The framework factorizes a Bayesian model according to RAG information flow, distinguishes task success from generator success, analyzes annotation allocation, and models LLM-as-a-judge outputs as calibrated noisy observations.
AI.result: Across 27 RAG configurations covering three datasets, three retrievers, and three generators, conditional decomposition exposes substantial differences among systems with similar marginal metrics. Retrieval-success labels are more informative than task-success labels for estimating policy adherence.
AI.conclusion: Joint probabilistic evaluation gives a more diagnostic account of RAG behavior and can combine limited human judgments with cheaper automated assessments.

title: Benchmarking and Boosting Multilingual Capabilities of LVLMs via OCR-Centric Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: PM4Bench enables parallel 10-language evaluation of LVLMs and identifies visual-text OCR as a major source of cross-lingual disparity. OCR-centric GRPO with synthetic label-free data improves multilingual VQA and reduces that disparity.
AI.motivation: Non-parallel multilingual benchmarks confound model limitations with dataset differences, and visually rendered text creates poorly understood cross-lingual gaps.
AI.method: Build a strictly parallel multimodal 10-language, multi-task benchmark with a text-in-image setting, then train with GRPO on fully synthesized label-free OCR data.
AI.result: Experiments on 10 LVLMs identify OCR as a key driver of disparity; the trained model improves multilingual VQA, reduces vision-setting gaps, and transfers beyond PM4Bench.
AI.conclusion: Label-free OCR-focused RL provides an efficient route to more equitable multilingual LVLM deployment.

title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Translation Quality Estimation in LRMs through Mutually Boosting Implicit and Explicit Reasoning

AI.tldr: RIEQE jointly improves implicit and explicit reasoning for fine-grained translation quality estimation through non-thinking SFT followed by RLVR. Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 surpasses all baselines for explicit reasoning on WMT tests.
AI.motivation: LRMs have multilingual ability but still struggle to learn fine-grained QE, even with long reasoning chains.
AI.method: Decompose QE into subtasks, apply NonThinking-SFT to strengthen layer-wise implicit reasoning, then Thinking-RLVR to improve token-wise explicit reasoning.
AI.result: RIEQE leads all baselines in explicit reasoning on WMT and its implicit reasoning matches the best current encoder-based models.
AI.conclusion: Implicit and explicit reasoning can improve each other bidirectionally for fine-grained QE.

title: Source-Grounded Semantic Reinforcement Learning for Low-Resource Target-Language Generation

AI.tldr: SG-SRL converts abundant source-language monolingual data into cross-lingual semantic supervision for low-resource generation. It improves Chinese-to-Thai generation and supports Chinese-to-Tibetan with a contrastively trained encoder reward.
AI.motivation: Low-resource target generation lacks parallel data, while source-language monolingual data is difficult to exploit through standard SFT.
AI.method: Optimize source-language data with reference-free RL using a cross-lingual semantic reward, then use lightweight supervised recovery to restore output form.
AI.result: SG-SRL outperforms cold-start SFT, source-only continued pretraining, and synthetic-data SFT on Chinese-to-Thai; human preferences and training-independent metrics corroborate gains.
AI.conclusion: Semantic RL plus recovery can use monolingual data effectively, though success depends on reward-model discrimination.

title: TEMPO: Temporally-grounded Multi-task Post-training for Large Audio-Language Models

AI.tldr: TEMPO is a unified audio, speech, and music timestamping model trained with temporally grounded SFT and GRPO refinement. It outperforms Audio Flamingo Next and Qwen3-Omni on a new benchmark.
AI.motivation: LALMs can describe clips but generally cannot timestamp identified events, speakers, or sounds.
AI.method: Use atomic timestamp tokens, a wall-clock time-aware projector, and a distance-aware Gaussian loss in synthetic-to-real SFT; refine with GRPO and verifiable temporal rewards.
AI.result: On a 10K-sample benchmark across five tasks, TEMPO outperforms two timestamp-trained LALMs; SFT provides most gains and GRPO adds consistent moderate improvements.
AI.conclusion: Temporally grounded multi-task SFT is the main driver of unified audio timestamping performance, with RL as a useful refinement.

title: The Dialect Tax: Dialectal Biases Persist throughout the Language Modeling Pipeline

AI.tldr: This study finds that the dialect tax persists through tokenization, pre-training, post-training, and inference rather than arising from one pipeline stage. Character-level tokenization does not remove dialectal asymmetries or accuracy gaps.
AI.motivation: Dialectal performance gaps are known, but their sources across the language-modeling pipeline are unclear.
AI.method: Compare semantically parallel English dialect and SAE texts across pipeline stages, including a character-level tokenizer counterfactual, gradient analysis, and reward-model evaluation.
AI.result: Dialect pairs produce more divergent pre-training gradients than unrelated SAE documents; reward models show contextual and unstable dialect preferences.
AI.conclusion: Dialectal inequity is accumulated across the full language-modeling pipeline and needs multi-stage remedies.

title: Lifelong Intent Discovery: A Continual Learning Protocol and Method

AI.tldr: The paper formalizes Continual Open-Stream Intent Discovery and introduces a stream-construction protocol plus the memory-augmented CIDA agent. CIDA outperforms existing baselines on constructed ClincCL and BankCL streams.
AI.motivation: New intent discovery must adapt continually, but prior work largely omits continual hybrid-stream settings.
AI.method: Define COSID, transform static datasets into temporally partitioned open streams, add evaluation metrics, and use CIDA to screen data, cluster new intents, and expand LLM-generated memory.
AI.result: Experiments validate both the protocol's expressiveness and CIDA's superiority over baselines on ClincCL and BankCL.
AI.conclusion: COSID and CIDA provide a configurable foundation for continual discovery of historical and emerging intents.

title: VIB-Simp: IB-Inspired Output-Logit Regularization for German Text Simplification

AI.tldr: VIB-Simp regularizes output-logit mean and variance to improve German text simplification while preserving meaning. It consistently improves SARI across five model families.
AI.motivation: Standard fine-tuning imitates references but does not directly control the predictive distributions that determine lexical complexity.
AI.method: Apply a closed-form Gaussian KL surrogate to output logits, optionally combined with an unlikelihood lexical penalty for difficult candidates.
AI.result: On TextComplexityDE and 20Min, VIB-Simp improves SARI for LLaMA-3.2-3B, Qwen-2.5-3B, mBART, GerPT-2, and mGPT; analyses rule out shortening and dictionary-only explanations.
AI.conclusion: IB-style output-logit control can retain meaning-critical content while suppressing unnecessary lexical complexity.

title: Lexical Perturbations Disrupt LLM Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Attention Diversion

AI.tldr: Character-level corruption substantially damages LLM reasoning because fragmented subword tokens divert attention, while filler insertion has little effect. Restoring both token content and attention is needed for substantial recovery.
AI.motivation: The robustness of LLM reasoning to realistic lexical corruption is poorly understood.
AI.method: Test open-weight and frontier models on four reasoning benchmarks under keyboard noise, character swaps, and filler insertion, with attention analyses and factorial restoration interventions.
AI.result: Fragmentation, not length, drives accuracy loss; attention diversion concentrates in middle and final layers, and single-channel repairs fail consistently.
AI.conclusion: Lexical corruption jointly damages content and attention, limiting inference-time repair methods that address only one mechanism.

title: QUBRIC: Co-Designing Queries and Rubrics for RL Beyond Verifiable Rewards

AI.tldr: QUBRIC co-designs evaluable queries and rubrics for RL beyond verifiable rewards. It improves ArenaHard by 5.5 points over SFT and transfers by 6.3 points on average to held-out reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Rubric-based RL is constrained by fixed query distributions: open queries yield vague rubrics while naively narrow ones can create unverifiable fabricated references.
AI.method: Rewrite prompts using teacher key points, generate contrastive rubrics from teacher-policy gaps, filter learnable query-rubric pairs, and train with GRPO.
AI.result: QUBRIC gains 5.5 points on ArenaHard and, trained only on instruction-following data, averages 6.3-point gains on legal, moral, and narrative reasoning benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Joint query-rubric design makes rubric-based RL practical beyond strictly verifiable tasks.

title: Learning to Evict: Policy-Driven KV Cache Optimization for Multi-Hop Multimodal Spatial Reasoning

AI.tldr: ScoutKV learns per-head KV-cache eviction policies for multi-hop multimodal spatial reasoning. It reduces FLOPs, latency, and peak memory while maintaining or improving accuracy.
AI.motivation: Interleaved visual and textual tokens make the KV cache grow rapidly over multi-hop visualization-of-thought reasoning.
AI.method: Train a lightweight per-KV-head policy using key-value features, positional and modality embeddings, offline attention-target SFT, and online GRPO with multimodal process rewards.
AI.result: ScoutKV consistently lowers computational cost, latency, and peak memory across multimodal spatial reasoning benchmarks and generalizes to broader vision-language tasks.
AI.conclusion: RL-based long-term token-utility prediction can make multi-hop multimodal reasoning more scalable.

title: Mitigating Forgetting Between Supervised and Reinforcement Learning Yields Stronger Reasoners

AI.tldr: MIFO prevents catastrophic forgetting between SFT and RL in reasoning post-training through selective data use and temporary freezing of RL-critical parameters. It reaches SOTA with 1.5% of prior SFT data and 20.4% of prior RL data.
AI.motivation: Large, redundant SFT updates can overwrite small non-robust RL updates in combined SFT+RL pipelines.
AI.method: Interleave RL with challenging SFT samples selected by rollout accuracy, optimize high-entropy SFT tokens, and freeze parameters identified as RL-critical during SFT.
AI.result: MIFO attains SOTA reasoning with far less data than prior SOTA methods and generates traces up to 10 times shorter than standard SFT-to-RL training.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly protecting RL-learned parameters and focusing SFT can improve stability, efficiency, and reasoning quality.

title: SurgMind-R1: Overcoming Reasoning Collapse in Surgical Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: SurgMind-R1 addresses reasoning collapse in surgical VLMs through reasoning data, staged SFT, and GRPO. It significantly outperforms prior VLMs on complex SurgLite-Bench inference and retains high direct no-think accuracy.
AI.motivation: Answer-only SFT can erase explicit surgical reasoning, while expert chain-of-thought data are expensive to build.
AI.method: Construct Cholec-Think with expert and VLM-assisted rationales, perform domain-adaptive and reasoning-enhanced SFT, then apply GRPO with rule-based structured-thinking rewards.
AI.result: The model leads on complex SurgLite-Bench inference, supports high-accuracy no-think inference, and shows zero-shot OOD generalization.
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement-enforced structured reasoning can improve traceable surgical scene understanding without sacrificing real-time use.

title: Accelerating Constrained Decoding with Token Space Compression

AI.tldr: CFGzip compresses the token search space for CFG-constrained decoding offline, cutting constrained-decoding latency by up to 75x. It reduces overhead to about 1.2-2x on the hardest grammars.
AI.motivation: CFG decoding searches the full vocabulary at every step, making complex grammar constraints prohibitively expensive.
AI.method: Apply an offline token-space compression technique that reduces the candidate space used by CFG engines.
AI.result: Batched inference achieves up to 75x lower latency, enabling scalable constrained decoding for complex CFGs.
AI.conclusion: Token-space compression removes a key computational barrier to large-scale structured LLM generation.

title: OLIVIA: Online Learning via Inference-time Action Adaptation

AI.tldr: OLIVIA adapts LLM tool-use decisions online with a contextual linear bandit over hidden states, without backbone fine-tuning. It outperforms prompt-based online adaptation and contextual-bandit variants on four tool-use benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing online adaptation changes prompts or memory but leaves the action-selection layer fixed and lacks action-level credit assignment and uncertainty-aware exploration.
AI.method: Replace the frozen action head with per-action contextual linear bandits, use LinUCB exploration, and update sufficient statistics from step feedback with Sherman-Morrison updates.
AI.result: Across ToolBench, TaskBench, TaskBench-MM, BFCL, Qwen3-4B, and Mistral-7B, OLIVIA improves over compared adaptation methods with negligible inference overhead.
AI.conclusion: Direct inference-time adaptation of the action-selection layer can efficiently improve LLM tool-use policies.

title: Auditing LLM Benchmarks with Item Response Theory

AI.tldr: An Item Response Theory indicator audits frozen LLM benchmark labels and finds likely mislabels with 95% precision in its top 200 cases. It also reveals reward-model specialization and a possible contaminated or over-optimized frontier model.
AI.motivation: Benchmark label errors propagate silently into downstream benchmarks and distort evaluation.
AI.method: Fit an Item Response Theory indicator using results from 114 models across seven preference and multiple-choice benchmarks.
AI.result: The indicator reaches 95% precision among its top 200 flagged labels, outperforming a supervised classifier; one frontier reward model agrees with detected mislabels 78% of the time versus 38% for peers.
AI.conclusion: IRT-based auditing can expose inherited errors, ambiguous items, and model-specific benchmark pathologies.

title: EST-PRM: Stress-Testing Process Reward Models Before They Become Load-Bearing

AI.tldr: EST-PRM stress-tests process reward models under label-preserving reasoning transformations and finds substantial model-specific vulnerabilities. Mitigations involve trade-offs between robustness coverage and false positives.
AI.motivation: PRMs are used as dense correctness signals without sufficient validation that their scores remain stable under equivalent reasoning rewrites.
AI.method: Evaluate step inflation, dependency-aware reordering, and confidence markers; decompose vulnerability into reward inflation and correctness-sensitivity loss.
AI.result: Across 4,687 chains, Math-Shepherd has a 0.139 plus or minus 0.031 correlation drop and 29.7 plus or minus 4.2% score inflation, while Qwen2.5-Math-PRM reaches 47.6 plus or minus 4.3% inflation under step inflation.
AI.conclusion: PRMs need robustness auditing before they are used as load-bearing process supervision.

title: UserRL: A Gym-Based Testbed for User-Centric Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: UserRL is a gym-based testbed for user-centric multi-turn RL with simulated users and flexible turn- and trajectory-level rewards. Experiments identify effective cold starts, reward-to-go scoring, and simulator strength as important factors.
AI.motivation: Agent value depends on serving diverse and evolving user goals, but reproducible user-centric RL studies are limited.
AI.method: Provide standardized gym environments with simulated users and decouple turn-level reward shaping from trajectory-level scoring.
AI.result: Across Qwen3 models, SFT cold start is effective, trajectory-level reward-to-go improves effectiveness and efficiency, and stronger simulators improve training while open-source simulators transfer positively.
AI.conclusion: UserRL offers a practical controlled foundation for training and evaluating interactive user-centric agents.

title: CALIBURN: Self-Calibrated LLM Unlearning Alignment

AI.tldr: CALIBURN calibrates unlearning gradients using a model's confidence in undesirable knowledge, enabling finer forgetting control with better utility retention. It improves the removal-utility trade-off on benchmarks including MUSE and WMDP.
AI.motivation: Gradient-ascent unlearning causes catastrophic forgetting, alignment-based alternatives depend on reference quality, and both often need large retention datasets.
AI.method: Quantify target-model confidence in undesirable knowledge and use it to calibrate unlearning gradient updates.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show effective unlearning and improved knowledge-removal versus utility-preservation trade-offs compared with state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Confidence-calibrated updates can reduce retention-data dependence while making LLM unlearning more precise.

title: Spectral DPO: Mitigating Validation Collapse via Heavy-Tailed Regularization

AI.tldr: Spectral DPO uses heavy-tailed regularization of LoRA effective spectra to prevent validation collapse during preference optimization. It gains 2.33-2.42 points over the strongest baseline and sustains accuracy for ten epochs where vanilla DPO degrades.
AI.motivation: Preference-reward optimization can improve while downstream reasoning, factuality, or safety worsens, and its relationship to weight-space geometry is unclear.
AI.method: Add a stochastic spectral penalty based on truncated top-k Lanczos estimates that controls tail exponent, largest singular-direction growth, and match to a heavy-tailed target.
AI.result: Across ten seeds, three model families, and five benchmarks, Spectral DPO improves by 2.33-2.42 points; controls rule out norm clipping, KL anchoring, and length inflation.
AI.conclusion: Effective-spectrum control under rank-64 LoRA can mitigate reward overoptimization, though no single causal statistic is established.

title: Labels have Human Values: Value Calibration of Subjective Tasks

AI.tldr: MC-STL models latent human value groups to calibrate subjective NLP predictions conditionally on those values. It outperforms baselines and achieves multicalibration across diverse subjective-task datasets.
AI.motivation: Subjective labels reflect legitimate value disagreement, but models often ignore latent values and become miscalibrated across value classes.
AI.method: Infer value groups from rationales, taxonomies, or annotator descriptors and learn value-group-specific representations with value-conditional calibration.
AI.result: On toxic conversation, value reasoning, T2I-safety, and preference-alignment datasets, MC-STL consistently improves probabilistic prediction while achieving multicalibration.
AI.conclusion: Explicit value structure is necessary for calibrated learning from pluralistic subjective labels.

title: AdaMame: A Training Recipe for Adaptive Multilingual Reasoning

AI.tldr: AdaMame trains LRMs to reason in the query language without sacrificing mathematical accuracy. Across two benchmarks, two LRMs, and 12 languages, AdaMame-GRPO achieves Pareto-optimal accuracy, language fidelity, and token efficiency.
AI.motivation: LRMs often collapse to English or code-switch during multilingual reasoning, while binary language rewards create accuracy and efficiency trade-offs.
AI.method: First SFT on non-machine-translated traces in five languages, then apply GRPO with a progressively increasing query-conditioned language-alignment factor.
AI.result: AdaMame-GRPO outperforms all baselines on the three-way trade-off, with strongest gains on out-of-domain lower-resource languages.
AI.conclusion: Gradually shifting from multilingual exploration to query-language exploitation improves multilingual reasoning alignment.

title: SCRIBE: Learning Reusable Skill Rubrics for Process Reward Models

AI.tldr: SCRIBE learns reusable subgoal-level rubrics for process rewards in tool-augmented agent training. It raises Qwen3-4B AIME25 from 43.3% to 63.3% and improves across math reasoning and tool-use benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Multi-step agent training has difficult credit assignment, while LLM judges are inconsistent and existing rubrics are instance-specific and reference-dependent.
AI.method: Decompose trajectories into subgoals, cluster behaviors into reusable Skill Prototypes, and score using prototype-level criteria.
AI.result: SCRIBE consistently exceeds strong RL and rubric-based reward baselines, reduces reference-answer dependence, and gives more stable cross-instance judgments.
AI.conclusion: Reusable skill rubrics offer scalable and reliable process-level verification for tool-augmented agents.

title: Integrated and Cross-Architecture Interpretation of LLM Reasoning

AI.tldr: IAR combines output-layer and cross-layer probes to interpret LLM reasoning across architectures. Experiments on six models and four domains support its generalizable interpretability capability.
AI.motivation: Observable outputs do not reveal underlying reasoning patterns, and isolated probes can underestimate inferential structure.
AI.method: Identify crucial tokens with bandwidth-calibrated MIP and Tukey IQR detection, compare them with DTR-deep tokens across layers, and assess stability with Jaccard scores.
AI.result: Evaluations across mathematics, code, logic, and common sense demonstrate cross-architecture interpretation capability.
AI.conclusion: Integrating complementary token and layer probes can give a broader view of LLM reasoning patterns.

title: HumorGen: Cognitive Synergy for Humor Generation in Large Language Models via Persona-Based Distillation

AI.tldr: HumorGen uses six cognitive personas to synthesize theory-grounded humor data for a 7B model. Its variants outperform larger instruction-tuned baselines and remain competitive with frontier proprietary systems.
AI.motivation: Next-token training conflicts with the surprise and incongruity needed for humor, and it is unclear whether alignment or data design is more important.
AI.method: Use a Mixture-of-Thought framework with six psychology-inspired personas to create humor data, fine-tune a 7B student, and compare DPO and O-GRPO.
AI.result: Neither DPO nor O-GRPO improves over SFT, whereas HumorGen achieves top-tier open-weight performance.
AI.conclusion: Cognitive data curation matters more than alignment algorithms or model scale for humor generation.

title: Batch-of-Thought: Cross-Instance Learning for Enhanced LLM Reasoning

AI.tldr: Batch-of-Thought jointly processes related queries to exploit cross-instance reasoning signals without training. Its BoT-R variant improves accuracy and confidence calibration while cutting inference cost by up to 61%.
AI.motivation: Independent query processing discards shared reasoning patterns and consistency constraints across related instances.
AI.method: Compare related queries to identify templates and errors, implemented through a multi-agent reflection architecture with a joint-evaluation Reflector.
AI.result: Across three model families and six benchmarks, BoT-R consistently improves accuracy and calibration and reduces inference costs by up to 61%.
AI.conclusion: Batch-aware reasoning can improve both reliability and efficiency by using cross-instance information.

title: KnowMeBenchV2: Evidence-Grounded Person-Centric Long-Video Understanding

AI.tldr: KnowMeBenchV2 evaluates evidence-grounded person-centric long-video understanding across 327 videos and 3,061 questions. Its diagnostic shows that audiovisual evidence construction and cross-episode organization are crucial before answer generation.
AI.motivation: Existing long-video benchmarks do not isolate person-centric evidence sufficiency, temporal comparison, cross-episode synthesis, and grounded abstention.
AI.method: Build an evaluation-only benchmark over five multi-episode series with four evidence scopes and a matched grounded-abstention task; compare evidence routes under a fixed Qwen3.5-9B answerer.
AI.result: Humans score 78.0 on cross-episode synthesis; ASR-Retrieval scores 2.7 while KnowMe scores 64.9 under the diagnostic setup.
AI.conclusion: Strong long-video person understanding requires organized audiovisual evidence, not merely textualized retrieval before an answerer.

title: SPEC-Distill: Towards Efficient Speculative Distillation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

AI.tldr: SPEC-Distill uses offline teacher trajectories as speculative prefixes during RLVR, reducing online teacher cost and fresh rollout generation. It improves Qwen3-4B average accuracy from 66.1 to 73.2 over GRPO.
AI.motivation: RLVR needs costly long rollouts, and on-policy distillation requires online large-teacher scoring at every RL step.
AI.method: Build an offline expert-trajectory pool, accept a lenience-controlled speculative prefix, complete it with the student policy, and update only through standard GRPO verifiable rewards.
AI.result: SPEC-Distill outperforms OPD at two scales; for Qwen3-1.7B it matches Luffy accuracy while cutting rollout tokens by about 60% and time from 10.90 to 7.06 hours.
AI.conclusion: Early teacher-prefix scaffolding offers an efficient balance between expert guidance and on-policy exploration.

title: ConsensusBench: Benchmark of Consensus Nodes for LLM Reasoning via Outcome Reward Densifying

AI.tldr: ConsensusBench supplies rule-based process signals from clustered intermediate conclusions, and ConsensusPR densifies GRPO outcome rewards. The method consistently surpasses GRPO-style approaches across five reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Final-answer-only rewards become too sparse for long, complex reasoning trajectories.
AI.method: Filter correct rollouts, cluster equivalent intermediate statements into Consensus Nodes, derive process rewards, and evaluate with accuracy, Node Coverage Rate, and Tokens per Node.
AI.result: Experiments on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, GSM8K, MATH-500, and ConsensusBench consistently exceed GRPO-style methods.
AI.conclusion: Consensus intermediate conclusions provide practical process supervision for long-horizon LLM reasoning.

title: VectorGym: A Multi-Task Benchmark for SVG Code Generation, Sketching and Editing

AI.tldr: VectorGym is a human-annotated four-task benchmark for SVG generation, sketching, editing, and captioning. Its GRPO-trained Qwen3-VL 8B baseline surpasses Qwen3-VL 235B and matches GPT-4o among evaluated systems.
AI.motivation: Existing SVG benchmarks lack realistic, challenging professional-design workflows and often depend on synthetic edits.
AI.method: Release VG-Sketch, VG-Edit, VG-Text, and VG-Cap with expert annotations, plus curriculum multi-task GRPO using rendering rewards and a human-validated VLM-as-a-Judge metric.
AI.result: The Qwen3-VL 8B baseline reaches open-source SOTA, exceeds Qwen3-VL 235B, and matches GPT-4o; frontier VLM evaluation reveals major gaps.
AI.conclusion: VectorGym provides a rigorous, professionally aligned framework for advancing visual code generation.

title: Skill Reuse as Compression in Agentic RL

AI.tldr: ReuseRL improves agentic RL generalization by compressing successful trajectories into reusable skills under an MDL objective. It improves in- and out-of-distribution success on ALFWorld, TextWorld-Cooking, and Countdown-Stepwise.
AI.motivation: RL-trained LLM agents often learn brittle task-specific shortcuts rather than reusable structure.
AI.method: Extract a shared skill dictionary from successful trajectories and add a segmentation cost that penalizes idiosyncratic, poorly compressible behavior; derive a PAC-Bayes bound.
AI.result: ReuseRL exceeds vanilla GRPO and strong round-length baselines on all three environments for both in- and out-of-distribution success.
AI.conclusion: Structural compressibility and skill reuse can serve as a useful inductive bias for robust agent generalization.

title: Token-weighted Direct Preference Optimization with Attention

AI.tldr: AttentionPO is a content-aware Token-weighted DPO method that uses the model's own attention to weight response tokens. It improves AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, and ArenaHard beyond existing preference-optimization methods.
AI.motivation: DPO weights every response token equally, while prior token-level methods use brittle position heuristics or costly separate models.
AI.method: Formulate TwDPO and instantiate it as AttentionPO, prompting the LLM as a pairwise judge and using its comparison attention to estimate token importance with two extra forward passes.
AI.result: AttentionPO significantly improves performance on AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, and ArenaHard over existing preference-optimization approaches.
AI.conclusion: Self-attention can provide efficient content-sensitive token valuation for preference optimization.

title: Two to Tango: Coupled Task-Reference Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning

AI.tldr: DualSelect jointly selects safety references and compatible downstream task samples to preserve safety during LLM fine-tuning. It improves REDORCA Safety Avg. by at least 5.10 points over the strongest baseline.
AI.motivation: Downstream adaptation can erode safety, while fixed safety examples, global constraints, and one-sided task filtering ignore task-specific safety conflicts.
AI.method: Refresh task-conditioned safety references, select high-preservation-loss and high-conflict references with entropy-regularized minimax surrogates, then filter compatible task samples with gradient correction.
AI.result: Across English instruction-following and math settings on 1B-8B models, DualSelect preserves safety while retaining utility and ranks highest in Safety Avg. across judges with moderate overhead.
AI.conclusion: Coupled reference and task selection better manages the safety-utility trade-off during fine-tuning.

title: Culturally-Aware Alignment for Multimodal Models via Group Reward Optimization for Southeast Asia

AI.tldr: The work introduces SEA-Omni benchmarks and MERaLiON-Omni-10B for culturally aware Southeast Asian multimodal modeling. The resulting model performs strongly on SEA benchmarks while maintaining reasonable general capabilities.
AI.motivation: MLLMs have Western bias and insufficiently reflect Southeast Asian languages, code-switching, and cultural multimodal cues.
AI.method: Assemble SEA-focused image and video datasets, train MERaLiON-Omni-10B progressively, and use GRPO with fact-anchored dual rewards for cultural density and multimodal coherence.
AI.result: Experimental results indicate strong SEA benchmark performance with reasonable general capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Region-specific evaluation and fact-anchored cultural alignment can improve multimodal models for Southeast Asia.

title: AlphaToken: Decoupling Adaptation and Stability for Path-Aware Response Token Valuation in LLM Post-Training

AI.tldr: AlphaToken selects response tokens for post-training by separately valuing task adaptation and capability stability along direct and causal paths. It improves post-training performance and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.
AI.motivation: Existing token-selection methods rely on local heuristics and lack an optimization-guided proxy for response-token value.
AI.method: Combine local-gradient direct-path and autoregressive causal-path signals, approximate stability using a reference-anchored Fisher-drift proxy, and efficiently compute token values with Ghost Dot-Product.
AI.result: Masking low-value response tokens during fine-tuning and preference optimization improves performance and reduces forgetting.
AI.conclusion: Path-aware token valuation can concentrate post-training on positions that improve adaptation without sacrificing retained capabilities.

title: Support Vector Rubrics: Closing the Gap Between Self-Generated and Human Rubrics

AI.tldr: Support Vector Rubrics constructs discriminative rubric banks from preference data using max-margin learning. It reduces the RubricBench gap to human rubrics from 24.1 to 0.3 points and transfers across judges.
AI.motivation: Self-generated rubrics describe good responses but do not discriminate closely matched candidates as effectively as human criteria.
AI.method: Mine contrastive features into a rubric bank, learn a prompt-conditioned selector and global weights, then refine via support-pair selection and adversarial hard-negative probing.
AI.result: SVR outperforms strong self-rubric and judge baselines on RubricBench, transfers across judges without retraining, and remains competitive on RewardBench, RM-Bench, and dedicated reward models.
AI.conclusion: Boundary-defining rubrics are a principled way to close the gap between self-generated and human evaluation criteria.

title: PALMs: Using Multi-Construct Grounded Rationales for Modeling Population Preferences in LLMs

AI.tldr: PALMs aligns separate models to the preferences of five national populations using psychology- and culture-grounded rationales. It yields 8.59% average relative improvement over the best baseline and transfers to downstream preference tasks.
AI.motivation: Population simulation requires modeling systematic variation in values, beliefs, and cultural norms, not only individual behavior or surface demographics.
AI.method: Synthesize rationales grounded in psychological and cultural constructs and use them as latent supervision for population-specific preference tuning.
AI.result: Across personality, values and beliefs, norms, and morality, PALMs improves 8.59% on average; it also improves personalized reward modeling by 5.19% and population simulation by 6.34%.
AI.conclusion: Construct-grounded rationales provide a richer preference-learning signal than demographic prompting or survey-based fine-tuning.

title: KG-RLVR: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning with Knowledge Graph-Derived Process Rewards

AI.tldr: KG-RLVR derives locally computable process rewards from external knowledge-graph evidence for domain-specific LLM reasoning. It consistently improves over vanilla RL on medical and multi-domain QA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: High-quality reasoning trajectories and rationales are costly, difficult to verify, and hard to scale across knowledge-intensive domains.
AI.method: Retrieve graph evidence, consolidate noisy neighborhoods into representative evidence units, and reward coverage of relevant evidence plus selective integration of useful auxiliary evidence.
AI.result: KG-RLVR consistently improves vanilla RL across knowledge-intensive medical and multi-domain QA evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Traceable knowledge graphs can provide practical scalable process supervision without authored reasoning demonstrations.

title: SEAR: Self-Judging Agentic Reward Models

AI.tldr: SEAR trains agentic reward models to self-judge their own judging processes through dual-role adversarial co-evolution. It consistently improves reward-model reliability across diverse benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Agentic reward-model training is limited by coarse outcome supervision and expensive process-level annotations.
AI.method: Alternate a single model between judger and self-judger roles: optimize judging trajectories for self-judgment scores while training the self-judger to be critical and discriminative.
