AI.result: Extensive experiments show consistent reliability improvements across diverse benchmarks without relying on external human annotations.
AI.conclusion: Self-judging co-evolution can provide scalable process supervision for agentic reward models.

title: SPADER: Step-wise Peer Advantage with Diversity-Aware Exploration Rewards for Multi-Answer Question Answering

AI.tldr: SPADER improves long-horizon tool use for Multi-Answer QA with step-level peer advantages and diversity-aware exploration rewards. It generally improves recall and overall F1 on four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Multi-Answer QA needs both fine-grained credit assignment over long searches and exploration beyond frequent easy entities.
AI.method: Align parallel trajectories by decision step to compute critic-free Step-wise Peer Advantage, and reward rare discoveries while downweighting redundant ones.
AI.result: On QAMPARI, Mintaka, WebQSP, and QUEST, SPADER generally improves recall and F1 over prompting agents, outcome-supervised RL, and recent step-level supervision.
AI.conclusion: Combining peer-based step credit with diversity rewards promotes more complete multi-answer information seeking.

title: ProbeTQA: Verifiable Table Question Answering via Multi-Round Executable Probing

AI.tldr: ProbeTQA combines answer-first executable table probing with process-supervised RL for tool-free TableQA. Its 8B model reaches 65.8% on TableBench, exceeding GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-v3.2 by 13.4 and 6.8 points.
AI.motivation: Question-first synthesis creates logical hallucinations and standard RL gives sparse rewards for long TableQA reasoning chains.
AI.method: Generate instances from multi-round executable exploration with witness programs, convert verified code trajectories into natural-language traces and runtime-grounded rubrics, then train GRPO with a two-stage reward curriculum.
AI.result: The 8B model achieves tool-free SOTA on difficult benchmarks, including 65.8% TableBench accuracy and stated margins over GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-v3.2.
AI.conclusion: Execution-grounded generation and process rewards can internalize complex table reasoning without requiring tools at inference.

title: Entropy-Guided Token Dropout: Training Autoregressive Language Models with Limited Domain Data

AI.tldr: EntroDrop regularizes multi-epoch LLM adaptation by masking predictable low-entropy tokens. It outperforms standard regularizers from 0.6B to 8B parameters and remains robust over extended training.
AI.motivation: Repeated training on scarce domain data causes overfitting because quickly learned low-entropy tokens dominate optimization and high-entropy-token generalization declines.
AI.method: EntroDrop selectively drops low-entropy tokens during training and uses a curriculum schedule to adjust regularization strength with training progress.
AI.result: Across 0.6B to 8B models, EntroDrop consistently outperforms standard regularization baselines and sustains performance during extended multi-epoch training.
AI.conclusion: Aligning regularization with token-level learning dynamics can make LLM adaptation more effective in data-constrained domains.

title: PAGE: Progress-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Advantage for Long-Horizon GUI Agents

AI.tldr: PAGE improves small VLM GUI agents with automatic progress rewards and hierarchical advantages. An 8B SVLM reaches 79.3% average success across three long-horizon GUI scenarios, 16.0 points above GRPO.
AI.motivation: GRPO's binary outcomes provide no trajectory progress signal and uniform advantages assign credit without regard to subtask semantics.
AI.method: PAGE derives continuous progress rewards from successful trajectories, then combines progress-based inter-rollout advantages with LVLM-segmented and verified subtask-level intra-rollout advantages.
AI.result: PAGE achieves 79.3% average success with an 8B SVLM across three scenarios, improving 16.0 percentage points over GRPO and competing with evaluated closed-source LVLMs.
AI.conclusion: Progress-aware rewards and hierarchical credit assignment can substantially narrow the capability gap of cost-effective local GUI agents.

title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data

AI.tldr: A controlled study finds that Mixed SFT on no-CoT and long-CoT data exceeds next-chunk reasoning RL's post-RLVR ceiling while using over 60 times less compute.
AI.motivation: Prior comparisons with conventional SFT do not establish whether next-chunk RL itself, rather than exposure to no-CoT data, causes observed gains.
AI.method: The study compares next-chunk reasoning RL with Mixed SFT, a single supervised stage jointly using no-CoT worked solutions and long-CoT data.
AI.result: Mixed SFT has a higher post-RLVR performance ceiling with over 60x lower training compute, consistently for in-domain math and out-of-domain reasoning; higher pre-RLVR accuracy need not yield higher post-RLVR accuracy.
AI.conclusion: No-CoT training strategies should be assessed across the complete post-training pipeline, and simple mixed supervision can outperform next-chunk RL.

title: Risk-conditioned Fine-tuning of Large Language Models

AI.tldr: Risk-conditioned RLHF trains one LLM policy with a continuous inference-time control over risk aversion, avoiding separate models for fixed CVaR levels.
AI.motivation: Existing risk-averse RLHF optimizes CVaR at fixed risk levels and cannot change the desired degree of risk aversion at inference time.
AI.method: The framework conditions a single RLHF policy on a continuous risk-control input.
AI.result: Across multiple benchmarks, one risk-conditioned policy adapts to different inference-time risk levels.
AI.conclusion: A continuous risk interface enables more flexible, risk-aware LLM deployment without retraining or serving multiple policies.

title: GeoSID: Quantizer-Aware Geometric Shaping for Semantic IDs in Generative Recommendation

AI.tldr: GeoSID reshapes item embeddings before Semantic ID quantization while leaving the generative recommender unchanged. On RPG, it improves Recall@10 by up to 8.13% and NDCG@10 by 6.91%.
AI.motivation: Anisotropic pretrained item embeddings can mismatch the structured quantization spaces used for Semantic IDs, yet prior work treats the pre-tokenization geometry as fixed.
AI.method: GeoSID applies projected distribution matching before SID assignment in tokenizer-specific residual-quantization levels or OPQ/PQ blocks.
AI.result: On RPG, GeoSID gains up to 8.13% relative Recall@10 and 6.91% NDCG@10, while reducing projected discrepancy and prefix-level collisions and improving code-use balance.
AI.conclusion: Tokenizer-side geometric shaping improves Semantic ID quality and generative retrieval without modifying the downstream recommender.

title: RegionDoc-R1: Reinforcing Semantic Layout-Aware Reasoning for Document Understanding

AI.tldr: RegionDoc-R1 reinforces region-grounded document reasoning by predicting relevant RoIs and receiving step-wise feedback. It achieves state-of-the-art results across form understanding, table QA, and layout-sensitive extraction benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Document reasoning requires linking precise visual regions to answers, but existing approaches lack fine-grained region-level grounding supervision.
AI.method: RegionDoc-R1 combines RA-GRPO, the SR-Doc corpus with cross-page and region annotations, and Ada-CoT to dynamically adjust reasoning by task.
AI.result: Experiments on several document reasoning benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance on form understanding, table-based QA, and layout-sensitive information extraction.
AI.conclusion: Explicit RoI prediction and adaptive step-wise reasoning strengthen spatially grounded MLLM document understanding.

title: Tokenization as Structural Inductive Bias: Grapheme-Constrained Subwords for Multilingual Modeling and Vocabulary Surgery

AI.tldr: StructPiece is an unsupervised grapheme-constrained, affix-biased tokenizer that favors structural alignment over compression. Its vocabulary surgery recovers 89.4% of LLaMA-3.2-1B baseline X-CSQA reasoning performance after 2.6B tokens, versus 76.4% for naive BPE.
AI.motivation: Compression-oriented subword boundaries determine prediction units but may not reflect linguistic structure or support vocabulary adaptation.
AI.method: StructPiece enforces Unicode Extended Grapheme Cluster boundaries and biases merges toward corpus-induced affix patterns; it is also evaluated by replacing LLaMA-3.2-1B's 128k vocabulary with 32k tokens initialized by mean pooling.
AI.result: Across nine languages and five scripts, StructPiece has worse bits-per-character but lower matched-budget token perplexity; surgery recovers 89.4% versus 76.4% X-CSQA performance and yields higher embedding cosine coherence.
AI.conclusion: Token boundaries are a controllable structural inductive bias that can improve representation learning and multilingual vocabulary adaptation.

title: Robust Failure, Conservative Repair: Textual Knowledge Distillation from Cross-Model Failures

AI.tldr: RFCR distills only cross-model shared failure rules, sharpens their boundaries, and abstains when no rule helps. It raises BIG-Bench Hard cheat-sheet accuracy from 68.50% to 71.25% without hurting previously correct cases.
AI.motivation: Rules extracted from one model's failures can be model-specific or misapplied, destabilizing transfer to other model families.
AI.method: RFCR finds failures shared across models, derives rules from them, uses boundary cases to constrain rule application, and abstains when no useful rule is available.
AI.result: On 400 BIG-Bench Hard items, RFCR improves accuracy by 2.75 points to 71.25% (95% CI [+1.25,+4.50]) without degradation on previously correct cases.
AI.conclusion: Conservative, boundary-aware repair makes failure-derived textual knowledge more transferable across models.

title: S3Mem: Structured Spatiotemporal Scene-Event Memory for Long-Horizon Interactive Question Answering

AI.tldr: S3Mem stores heterogeneous histories as scene-event units and routes compact evidence packs for long-horizon QA. It reaches 0.48 F1 and 0.40 BLEU on LoCoMo using 1,073 evidence tokens, about 15.8x fewer than the reference.
AI.motivation: Existing memory interfaces are not designed to select compact, fixed-reader evidence from heterogeneous event, state, visual, temporal, and causal histories.
AI.method: S3Mem structures textual, visual, and agent-use histories into scene-event units; a router scores units, anchors, and anchor-support links for single- or short multi-hop evidence chains.
AI.result: It provides a strong score-token trade-off across LoCoMo, EMemBench Visual Games, and AMA-Bench; it has best F1 and second-best accuracy on EMemBench with 189 tokens and uses the fewest tokens on AMA-Bench.
AI.conclusion: Structured query-time memory routing can retain relevant long-horizon evidence while sharply reducing reader context.

title: InfoQuant: Shaping Activation Distributions for Low-Bit LLM Quantization

AI.tldr: InfoQuant is a train-free activation-shaping method for low-bit LLM quantization that uses PSOT and adaptive outlier-token selection. Under W4A4KV4, it retains about 97% of floating-point zero-shot accuracy on average.
AI.motivation: Existing PTQ methods smooth activations without specifying distributions suited to uniform low-bit quantization, leaving wide ranges or collapsed levels and high error.
AI.method: InfoQuant derives that favorable activations need both a small range and adequate dispersion, then applies Peak Suppression Orthogonal Transformation with adaptive outlier-token selection.
AI.result: Across multiple LLM families, InfoQuant outperforms prior PTQ and end-to-end training baselines and preserves approximately 97% of floating-point zero-shot accuracy under W4A4KV4.
AI.conclusion: Designing activations directly for the quantizer's distributional needs can improve low-bit LLM deployment.

title: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research

AI.tldr: MobileGym is a browser-hosted mobile-use simulator with deterministic JSON-state judging and highly parallel rollouts. GRPO on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct gains 12.8 points on its 256-task test set, retaining 95.1% of that gain on a 59-task real-device subset.
AI.motivation: Everyday mobile-agent research lacks controllable environments with verifiable outcomes and scalable, low-cost online RL.
AI.method: MobileGym represents, configures, forks, and compares full state as JSON, combines layered state with declarative tasks and programmatic judges, and provides MobileGym-Bench with structured AnswerSheet evaluation.
AI.result: One server hosts hundreds of 400 MB instances with 3-second cold starts; the benchmark has 416 task templates over 28 apps, and Sim-to-Real preserves 95.1% of the simulation training gain.
AI.conclusion: Deterministic state-based simulation can support reliable evaluation and large-scale RL for mobile GUI agents without proprietary backend replication.

title: MosaicAudio: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Controllable Video-to-Audio Generation

AI.tldr: MosaicAudio distills four specialist flow-matching teachers into one video-to-audio generator using dense, per-axis on-policy supervision. It achieves state-of-the-art compared-system performance on VGGSound and AudioCanvas, especially for complex multi-event scenes.
AI.motivation: A terminal aggregated RL reward entangles semantic, temporal, aesthetic, and spatial audio objectives, obscuring failures and causing competing axes to interfere.
AI.method: Four axis-specific teachers provide velocity fields along student-sampled denoising trajectories one axis at a time, while a perceptual manifold anchor maintains audio fidelity and limits reward hacking.
AI.result: On in-domain VGGSound and out-of-domain AudioCanvas, MosaicAudio leads compared V2A systems on objective metrics and human ratings, with consistent gains in complex multi-event scenes.
AI.conclusion: Dense, separated teacher feedback can align multiple conflicting V2A perceptual objectives in a single controllable model.

title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents

AI.tldr: LifeMem enables lifelong LLM agents to reuse experience by clustering trajectories into workflow-based skills and retrieving relevant skills and trajectories for new tasks. Across 10 environments and over 13k tasks, it reduces forgetting and improves transfer.
AI.motivation: Existing memory agents struggle to transfer reusable experience between environments and suffer catastrophic forgetting as memories accumulate.
AI.method: During learning, LifeMem clusters interaction trajectories by underlying workflows to extract skills; at inference, it recalls relevant skills and trajectories to guide actions.
AI.result: Experiments spanning 10 environments, over 13k tasks, and 2k new trajectories show reduced forgetting and superior cross-task transfer; consolidating structurally similar trajectories improves performance.
AI.conclusion: Workflow-structured memory supports continuing experience reuse, though task streaming affects lifelong learning outcomes.

title: Dense Process Supervision for Search Agents via Fact Utility Estimation

AI.tldr: This method supplies dense RL process supervision for search agents by estimating each retrieved fact's utility. It consistently outperforms baselines across seven single-hop and multi-hop QA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Outcome-only RL rewards do not clearly assign credit to intermediate search steps or distinguish their contributions to final answers.
AI.method: The approach extracts observations into a fact store, clusters equivalent facts, estimates cluster utility from group rollouts with Bayesian inference, and converts utility into step-level rewards.
AI.result: Across seven QA benchmarks, the method consistently outperforms existing baselines, with ablations showing clear relative multi-hop QA gains over outcome-reward-only training.
AI.conclusion: Fact-level utility estimation provides actionable dense credit signals for training search agents.

title: Anchoring What Matters: A Dual-Level Learning Framework for Visually-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning

AI.tldr: PIVOT strengthens visually grounded LVLM reasoning through calibrated replay and vision-guided token advantages, achieving highly competitive results across diverse benchmarks.
AI.motivation: On-policy RLVR discards valuable visually grounded trajectories after one update and distributes advantages uniformly, failing to reinforce critical perception and reasoning tokens.
AI.method: PIVOT selectively replays visually grounded experiences as optimization anchors and assigns extra vision-aware advantages based on tokens' local visual support and downstream impact.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks show highly competitive multimodal-reasoning performance.
AI.conclusion: Anchoring informative visual experiences and allocating credit by visual relevance can better preserve grounded reasoning behavior.

title: CAS: Conformalized Agentic Search via Adaptive Retrieval and Policy Weighting

AI.tldr: CAS combines conformal retrieval truncation with conformal confidence-weighted GRPO for reliable search agents. It improves QA accuracy while greatly reducing redundant tool calls across single-hop and multi-hop datasets.
AI.motivation: Fixed Top-K retrieval can lose critical evidence or admit noise, while progressive RL overconfidence causes hallucinations and unnecessary searches.
AI.method: CAS uses Adaptive Prediction Sets to choose dynamic document sets and Adaptive Conformal Inference to construct confidence sets that penalize low-confidence trajectories in GRPO.
AI.result: Experiments on single-hop and multi-hop QA show significantly higher reasoning accuracy and drastically fewer redundant tool invocations.
AI.conclusion: Conformal prediction can jointly improve retrieval and policy-training reliability for search agents.

title: Compute Allocation in Evolutionary Search: From Depth–Breadth to Multi-Armed Bandits

AI.tldr: BaSE allocates fixed LLM-call budgets across evolutionary-search trajectories with a multi-armed bandit. It improves mean fitness by 12.3% over the strongest island-protocol baseline across eight model-task settings.
AI.motivation: Evolutionary LLM search usually reports only best runs, leaving reliability and how to allocate a fixed call budget across depth and breadth unresolved.
AI.method: The study maps depth-breadth trade-offs over five models and three tasks, then uses the resulting regularities to motivate BaSE, a bandit allocation method across parallel trajectories.
AI.result: The analysis identifies a capability-gated fitness-compute envelope and task-specific bilinear depth-breadth interaction; BaSE improves mean fitness 12.3%, with greatest gains in high-variance settings.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive budget allocation alone can make LLM-guided evolutionary search more reliable without changing models, prompts, or evaluators.

title: Confidence Before Answering: A Paradigm Shift for Efficient LLM Uncertainty Estimation

AI.tldr: CoCA trains LLMs to state confidence before answering, jointly optimizing calibration and answer accuracy through segmented GRPO credit assignment. It improves calibration and uncertainty discrimination while preserving answer quality.
AI.motivation: Answer-first uncertainty methods estimate confidence only after a response, limiting practical use and tying confidence to a particular generated answer.
AI.method: CoCA separately rewards and assigns group-relative advantages to confidence and answer segments during GRPO, addressing reward hacking through segmented credit assignment.
AI.result: Across math, code, and factual QA benchmarks, CoCA improves calibration and uncertainty discrimination without sacrificing answer quality.
AI.conclusion: Confidence-first generation with separated training signals offers a practical uncertainty-estimation paradigm for LLMs.

title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety–Utility Balancing

AI.tldr: StepGuard is a guard model that audits completed agent trajectories and tool actions before execution, trained with automatically generated contrastive safe and unsafe trajectories. It reduces mean ASR by 77.3% on AgentDojo and AgentDyn with a 2.8-point utility drop.
AI.motivation: Tool-using agents risk file changes, data leakage, and unauthorized actions, while existing guardrails largely assess actions only after full trajectories complete.
AI.method: StepGen creates matched safe and unsafe trajectories at risky steps; StepGuard is trained with Balance-GRPO, which dynamically balances safe and unsafe learning by accuracy.
AI.result: StepGuard has the highest average accuracy among open-weight guard models and performance comparable to GPT-5.4; its guarded agents reduce mean ASR 77.3% relative to no guard with only 2.8 points lower utility.
AI.conclusion: Scalable step-level supervision can provide effective pre-execution tool-action guardrails with limited utility cost.

title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data

AI.tldr: EDIC trains LLMs to identify, classify, and act on each external-data instruction separately, following beneficial directives while rejecting prompt injections. It improves harmful rejection by up to 7.7% and Arena-Hard-Auto utility by 12.5% on Qwen3-4B.
AI.motivation: External data can mix legitimate instructions with adversarial injections, whereas defenses that trust or suppress all instructions force over-compliance or over-refusal.
AI.method: EDIC uses scene-grounded mixed-instruction data with counterfactual filtering and an SFT-initialized, GRPO-refined generative judge to give separately beneficial-compliance and harmful-compliance rewards.
AI.result: Across two backbones and five benchmarks, EDIC improves both safety and utility over the strongest prior defense, including up to 7.7% harmful-rejection and 12.5% utility gains.
AI.conclusion: Per-instruction credit attribution can improve both safety and usefulness when agents process untrusted external content.

title: RubricRM: Generative Reward Modeling via Dynamic Rubrics for Image Generation and Editing

AI.tldr: RubricRM generates input-specific evaluation rubrics before scoring image pairs for generation and editing. It outperforms specialized reward models and is competitive with strong proprietary MLLM judges despite smaller backbones.
AI.motivation: Fixed or scalar visual reward models cannot adapt their evaluation dimensions to different generation and editing instructions.
AI.method: RubricRM generates a rubric with dimensions, weights, and scoring criteria, then scores image candidates; separate generation and editing models use SFT followed by dimension-level-reward GRPO.
AI.result: On multiple text-to-image generation and image-editing benchmarks, RubricRM surpasses existing specialized reward models and remains competitive with strong proprietary MLLM judges.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic, instruction-specific rubrics improve reward-model interpretability and task sensitivity for visual generation.

title: HARVE: Hacking-Aware Reward-Head Vector Editing for Robust Reward Models

AI.tldr: HARVE is a training-free reward-head editing method that removes reward-model sensitivity to reward-hacking directions. Across eight reward models, it improves hacking robustness over fine-tuning baselines while preserving general capability.
AI.motivation: Scalar reward models are vulnerable to reward hacking, and training-based defenses can be costly or harm general reward-model capability.
AI.method: HARVE constructs a multidirectional hacking subspace from residual-stream directions in contrastive gold-hacked examples and projects its component out of the scalar reward-head vector.
AI.result: RewardHackBench covers 13 hacking patterns and exposes severe subcategory failures across eight models; HARVE improves robustness across these models and outperforms fine-tuning baselines.
AI.conclusion: Directly editing reward-head directions can robustly reduce reward hacking without gradient updates or fine-tuning.

title: Small Models, Fewer Heads, More Forgetting: Sparse Attention Fine-Tuning for SLM Continual Learning

AI.tldr: LightLoRA is a sparse, conflict-aware fine-tuning method for continual learning in small language models. It reaches state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks without adding parameters.
AI.motivation: SLMs have fewer attention heads and layers than LLMs, making prior representations easier to overwrite during continual learning.
AI.method: LightLoRA combines SVD-derived raw importance with gradient-direction task-conflict scores to select and update high-contribution, low-conflict attention heads.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance without extra parameters.
AI.conclusion: Sparsely updating attention heads chosen for importance and low conflict can preserve knowledge in continually trained SLMs.

title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation

AI.tldr: SecOPD provides token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning against adaptive prompt injection. Qwen3.6-27B achieves 9.0% ASR against PISmith versus 94.0% for Meta-SecAlign, and 4.7% on unseen agentic tool calling.
AI.motivation: Sequence-level DPO or GRPO feedback treats entire outputs equally, leaving defenses vulnerable to adaptive prompt injections with near-100% attack success rates.
AI.method: SecOPD scores tokens in an injected-input rollout using the initialization model conditioned on the corresponding clean input, yielding fine-grained on-policy distillation feedback.
AI.result: The defended Qwen3.6-27B has 9.0% ASR against PISmith versus 94.0% for Meta-SecAlign; in unseen agentic tool calling, ASR is 4.7% versus 5.5%.
AI.conclusion: Token-level defensive feedback can substantially improve robustness to adaptive prompt injection, including in unseen domains.

title: HLoRA: Hierarchical Regularization on Combined Parameter Space for LoRA Fine-Tuning

AI.tldr: HLoRA reduces LoRA catastrophic forgetting by regularizing importance in the combined weight-update space rather than separately over its factors. It improves adaptability while running about 20x faster and using 10% to 15% of prior methods' storage.
AI.motivation: Per-factor importance estimates for LoRA are unreliable because many B,A factor pairs can produce the same update BA.
AI.method: HLoRA computes path-integral importance over combined updates and applies element-wise preservation constraints plus layer-wise coefficients based on aggregate layer importance.
AI.result: On scientific, medical, and physical tasks with GPT-J and LLaMA-3, HLoRA mitigates forgetting while improving adaptability, running about 20x faster and requiring only 10% to 15% of prior storage.
AI.conclusion: Importance estimation in LoRA's actual update space enables efficient hierarchical continual-learning regularization.

title: APEx: Distillation of Agent Procedural Experience for Adaptive Deep Research Question Answering

AI.tldr: APEx combines trajectory memory with distilled procedural skills and test-time skill-guided RL for deep research agents. It surpasses GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points and the strongest memory baseline by 3.0 points across seven benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing deep-research experience methods either retrieve burdensome verbose traces or distill skills disconnected from policy adaptation.
AI.method: APEx links Executor, Distiller, and Planner modules in a closed loop, organizing histories into instance trajectories and category skills and optimizing them with three-stage alternating GRPO; skills guide regularized test-time RL.
AI.result: Across seven benchmarks, APEx achieves state-of-the-art results, exceeding GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points and the strongest memory-augmented baseline by 3.0 points.
AI.conclusion: Coupling procedural-skill distillation with online adaptation makes reusable deep-research experience more effective.

title: ANI: Adaptive Numerical Injection for Unifying Semantic and Arithmetic Representations in Numerical Reasoning

AI.tldr: ANI selectively injects numerical embeddings according to context to combine semantic handling of identifiers with precise arithmetic. It improves MATH performance by 9.5 points over the official reference model while retaining general linguistic performance.
AI.motivation: Text tokenization fragments numbers and hinders arithmetic, while context-agnostic numerical embeddings can corrupt numbers used as nominal identifiers.
AI.method: ANI uses a context-aware gate to inject FoNE numerical embeddings into latent representations for quantitative operands while preserving nominal identifiers.
AI.result: Across multiple LLMs, ANI improves MATH by 9.5 points over the official reference model and remains robust on general linguistic benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Context-selective numerical representation can unify semantic and arithmetic numerical reasoning.

title: The Straight and Narrow: Do LLMs Possess an Internal Moral Path?

AI.tldr: This work identifies a cross-lingual moral subspace in LLMs and uses Adaptive Moral Fusion to steer it at inference time. AMF reduces HarmBench jailbreak success while minimizing incorrect refusals on XSTest relative to standard baselines.
AI.motivation: RLHF-style behavioral guardrails may leave internal moral representations unaltered and vulnerable to complex jailbreaks.
AI.method: The authors validate a shared but culturally nuanced Chinese-English moral subspace with linear probes, extract causal Moral Vectors using Moral Foundations Theory, and dynamically fuse them at inference.
AI.result: AMF significantly lowers jailbreak success on HarmBench while minimizing incorrect refusals on XSTest compared with standard baselines.
AI.conclusion: Latent moral-space steering can provide a targeted intrinsic safety defense while balancing helpfulness.

title: Rubric-Aware Multi-Expert Online Policy Distillation for Chinese Elementary School Essay Writing

AI.tldr: RA-MOPD post-trains a 4B unified Chinese elementary-school essay writer with rubric-aware online distillation and cross-genre mixing. It reaches 4.21/5.00 and 97.8% routing on a 6,000-essay benchmark, within 0.09 of GPT-5.3 3-shot.
AI.motivation: Directly prompted frontier LLMs often choose the wrong genre or use an adult register for rubric-driven elementary-school writing.
AI.method: The four-stage pipeline uses Rubric-Weighted KL to emphasize reward-model-attributed rubric-critical tokens and parameter-free Cross-Genre Mixing guided by an empirical transfer prior.
AI.result: On a 6,000-essay benchmark with eight reward models, RA-MOPD scores 4.21/5.00 and 97.8% routing; a 1,200-essay teacher study gives it 62.8% preference, and it is statistically indistinguishable from a 4x-cost expert baseline.
AI.conclusion: Rubric-aware distillation can produce teacher-reviewable, age-appropriate multi-genre writing with a compact unified model.

title: DeepSearch-World: Self-Distillation for Deep Search Agents in a Verifiable Environment

AI.tldr: DeepSearch-Evolve self-distills web agents in DeepSearch-World, a deterministic environment with 420K multi-hop tasks. Its 9B model reaches 31.2% on BrowseComp, 61.5% on GAIA, and 93.4% on HotpotQA without stronger-model distillation.
AI.motivation: Fixed teacher trajectories limit supervised improvement, while sparse-reward RL is weak for long-horizon tool use.
AI.method: DeepSearch-Evolve iterates trajectory generation, filtering, data mixing, and fine-tuning in DeepSearch-World, which provides reproducible search and page-reading tools plus progress verification, reflection, and recovery.
AI.result: DeepSearch-World-9B attains 31.2% BrowseComp, 61.5% GAIA, and 93.4% HotpotQA, competitive with open-source agents without distillation from more capable models.
AI.conclusion: Large deterministic, verifiable environments can enable scalable self-evolution for deep-search agents.

title: ERR+: Sequential Entropy Resolution for Efficient and Decisive LLM Reasoning

AI.tldr: ERR+ trains reasoning models sequentially to resolve uncertainty in thinking traces and then improve response efficiency. Across five datasets, it consistently improves both accuracy and conciseness across model backbones.
AI.motivation: Correctness-only RLVR rewards do not optimize reasoning-process quality, despite correct traces showing larger and more frequent token-entropy drops than incorrect traces.
AI.method: Phase one applies Entropy Relief Reward to length-normalized cumulative thinking-phase entropy drops; phase two uses a within-group z-score relative-efficiency reward, separated because joint optimization creates early gradient conflict.
AI.result: Experiments on five datasets show consistent gains in accuracy and response conciseness across backbones.
AI.conclusion: Sequentially rewarding uncertainty resolution and relative efficiency can improve both the effectiveness and brevity of RLVR reasoning.

title: InterPol: De-anonymizing LM Arena via Interpolated Preference Learning

AI.tldr: INTERPOL de-anonymizes LM Arena responses by learning target-specific signatures from interpolated preference data. It improves Accuracy by 32% and AUROC by 25% on average over prior methods, and needs about 19% fewer interactions for equal ranking gain.
AI.motivation: Surface-style identity signals are unreliable for similar models and can be down-weighted in voting, leaving the anonymity risk inadequately characterized.
AI.method: INTERPOL creates controllable hard negatives by interpolating a target-mimicking copy model with its initial backbone, then trains a target detector with curriculum triplet preference learning.
AI.result: Across three frontier targets and two query sources, it gains 32% Accuracy and 25% AUROC on average; competitor-aware voting reduces interactions by about 69.9% relative to target-only voting.
AI.conclusion: Model-driven, interpolated preference data reveal a stronger response-anonymity risk for voting-based leaderboards.

title: PAC: Progress-Augmented Advantage Curriculum for Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning of LLMs

AI.tldr: PAC adaptively allocates multi-task LLM RL rollouts using both advantage-derived learnability and recent reward progress. It reaches comparable validation scores with fewer steps and achieves higher final averages than random and advantage-only curricula.
AI.motivation: Fixed task mixtures ignore changing task usefulness, while update-magnitude curricula can spend rollouts on large but ineffective updates.
AI.method: PAC combines task-level policy-update magnitude and recent reward gains in a Bayesian Thompson Sampling controller during GRPO training.
AI.result: In multi-level and multi-domain reasoning settings, PAC improves sample efficiency and final performance over random sampling and advantage-based curriculum baselines.
AI.conclusion: Tracking both potential learning signal and realized progress yields a more effective online post-training curriculum.

title: SCOPE: Signal-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation Enhancement with Dual-Path Adaptive Weighting

AI.tldr: SCOPE routes correct and incorrect on-policy rollouts to different adaptive supervision paths for reasoning alignment. It improves Avg@32 by 11.42% and Pass@32 by 7.30% on average over competitive baselines across six math benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Uniform teacher KL in on-policy distillation ignores differences in signal quality, while sparse outcome rewards make token-level credit assignment difficult.
AI.method: Incorrect trajectories receive teacher-perplexity-weighted KL, correct trajectories receive student-perplexity-weighted MLE, and both use group-level normalized weights.
AI.result: Across six mathematical-reasoning benchmarks, SCOPE achieves average relative gains of 11.42% in Avg@32 and 7.30% in Pass@32, with extended experiments indicating broader applicability.
AI.conclusion: Correctness-aware, quality-calibrated dual-path supervision improves on-policy reasoning distillation.

title: TRACER: An Information Entropy-Grounded Framework for Efficient Large-table Semantic Annotation

AI.tldr: TRACER compresses large tables into entropy-ranked, evidence-oriented contexts for semantic annotation, balancing annotation quality with inference efficiency against task-specific and LLM baselines.
AI.motivation: Full-table modeling is costly while aggressive filtering can discard semantic evidence needed to label columns and column pairs.
AI.method: TRACER ranks rows by ontology-related semantic uncertainty and uses hybrid compression, formalized as conditional-entropy minimization, before lightweight reading for type and property annotation.
AI.result: On several benchmarks, TRACER achieves a strong effectiveness-efficiency balance compared with task-specific and LLM baselines.
AI.conclusion: Information-entropy-grounded compression can preserve key table evidence for efficient semantic annotation.

title: LongAct: Harnessing Intrinsic Activation Patterns for Long-Context Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: LongAct performs saliency-guided sparse RL updates using weights linked to high-magnitude long-context query and key activations. It improves LongBench v2 by about 8% and generalizes better on RULER.
AI.motivation: Long-context RL has focused on rewards and data synthesis rather than intrinsic representations, despite sparse high-magnitude activations potentially identifying sensitive optimization components.
AI.method: LongAct selectively updates weights associated with high-magnitude query and key activations instead of applying uniform updates.
AI.result: The method improves LongBench v2 by approximately 8%, enhances RULER generalization, and consistently boosts performance under GRPO and DAPO; ablations support the saliency hypothesis.
AI.conclusion: Updating activation-salient components can unlock more effective and broadly applicable long-context RL.

title: EmoDap: Dual-Agent Prompt Retrieval Framework for Zero-Shot Fine-Grained Emotion Recognition

AI.tldr: EmoDap jointly trains a demonstration retriever and emotion predictor for zero-shot fine-grained emotion recognition. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Similarity retrieval for emotion ICL can add semantic noise and retrieve antonymous or otherwise counterproductive demonstrations.
AI.method: EmoDap builds a pseudo-labeled demonstration pool and contrastive emotion prototypes, then jointly optimizes retriever selection and prototype-guided prediction with GRPO.
AI.result: Across four benchmarks, EmoDap consistently exceeds state-of-the-art baselines using open-source LLM backbones.
AI.conclusion: Task-coupled retrieval and prototype-guided filtering improve robust zero-shot recognition of subtle emotions.

title: CRAM: Centroid-Routing and Adaptive MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

AI.tldr: CRAM is an adaptive Mixture-of-Experts approach for multimodal continual instruction tuning that isolates task patterns while reusing suitable experts. It outperforms existing methods across diverse benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Shared continual updates cause interference and forgetting, while allocating isolated modules per task is inefficient over long multimodal task streams.
AI.method: CRAM uses independent task-pattern modules, adaptive-rank expert instantiation, centroid-guided routing for reuse, and an orthogonality penalty for task-specific updates.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate superiority over existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive capacity allocation and centroid-based expert reuse can balance forgetting prevention with parameter efficiency in multimodal continual learning.

title: MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations

AI.tldr: MLLMCLIP transfers feature-level knowledge from a generative MLLM directly into a discriminative CLIP student, avoiding synthetic hard-negative generation. It achieves state-of-the-art compositional accuracy and improves zero-shot classification and retrieval.
AI.motivation: CLIP struggles with attribute-object and relational compositionality, while synthetic hard-negative pipelines require cascaded LLM and text-to-image generation.
AI.method: MLLMCLIP bridges teacher-student architectural differences through attention-based per-layer token selection and a CKA-based distillation loss.
AI.result: Compared with prior CLIP-enhancement approaches, MLLMCLIP obtains state-of-the-art compositional accuracy with consistent gains in standard zero-shot classification and image-text retrieval.
AI.conclusion: Direct heterogeneous feature distillation can strengthen both compositional and general vision-language representations without synthetic data.

title: CoDe-LoRA: Mitigating the Orthogonality Dilemma in Continual Learning of LLMs via Knowledge Consolidation and Decoupling

AI.tldr: CoDe-LoRA is a replay-free continual-learning method that separates universal knowledge consolidation from task-specific LoRA adaptation. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse continual-learning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Strict orthogonal LoRA projections prevent forgetting but also block transfer and accumulation of shared representations among related tasks.
AI.method: CoDe-LoRA combines adaptive null-space projection and semantic routing to consolidate universal knowledge while decoupling task-specific knowledge.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse continual-learning benchmarks show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Relaxing rigid parameter isolation through routed consolidation and decoupling better balances transfer with forgetting prevention.
